title.zh: 卷九 周本紀上第九: 太祖文帝 孝閔帝 世宗明帝
title.en: Volume 9 Northern Zhou Annals 1: Emperor Taizu Wen, Emperor Xianmin, Emperor Shizong Ming
title.raw: 卷九 周本紀上第九: 太祖文帝 孝閔帝 世宗明帝 Volume 9 Northern Zhou Annals 1: Emperor Taizu Wen, Emperor Xianmin, Emperor Shizong Ming

sentences.zh: 太祖文帝 孝閔帝 世宗明帝

translations.literal: Emperor Taizu Wen, Emperor Xiaomin, Emperor Shizong Ming.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizu Wen, Emperor Xiaomin, and Emperor Shizong Ming.

sentences.zh: 周太祖文皇帝姓宇文氏，諱泰，字黑獺，代郡武川人也。

translations.literal: The Grand Ancestor Emperor Wen of Zhou bore the surname Yuwen, taboo name Tai, style name Heita, and was a native of Wuchuan in Dai Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Ancestor Emperor Wen of Zhou had the surname Yuwen, taboo name Tai, style name Heita, and came from Wuchuan in Dai Commandery.

sentences.zh: 其先出自炎帝。

translations.literal: His ancestors traced back to Emperor Yan.
translations.idiomatic: His line descended from Emperor Yan.

sentences.zh: 炎帝為黃帝所滅，子孫遁居朔野。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yan was destroyed by Emperor Huang, his descendants fled to live in the northern wilds.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yan was overthrown by Emperor Huang, and his descendants withdrew into the northern frontier.

sentences.zh: 其後有葛烏兔者，雄武多算略。

translations.literal: Later there was Ge Wutu, bold and martial, skilled in stratagems.
translations.idiomatic: Later came Ge Wutu, a man of martial valor and many stratagems.

sentences.zh: 鮮卑奉以為主，遂總十二部落，世為大人及其裔孫曰普回，因狩得玉璽三紐，文曰「皇帝璽」，普回以為天授，己獨異之。

translations.literal: The Xianbei made him their leader; he gathered the twelve tribes and generation after generation served as the great chieftain. Among his descendants was Puhui, who while hunting obtained a jade seal with three loops inscribed "Imperial Seal." Puhui regarded it as heaven's grant and wondered at it alone.
translations.idiomatic: The Xianbei took him as their chief, and he united the twelve tribes, generation after generation serving as the great chieftain. A descendant named Puhui, while hunting, found a jade seal with three loops bearing the inscription "Imperial Seal." Puhui took it as a mandate from heaven and kept the wonder to himself.

sentences.zh: 其俗謂天子曰「宇文」，故國號宇文，並以為氏。

translations.literal: Their custom called the Son of Heaven "Yuwen," hence the state name Yuwen, also adopted as their clan name.
translations.idiomatic: In their custom the Son of Heaven was called "Yuwen," and so the state took the name Yuwen and the clan took it as their surname.

sentences.zh: 普回子莫那，自陰山南徙。

translations.literal: Puhui's son Monaj moved south of Yin Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Puhui's son Monaj migrated south of Yin Mountain.

sentences.zh: 始居遼西，是曰獻侯，為魏舅甥之國。

translations.literal: He first settled in Liaoxi; called the Marquis of Xian, his state became a relative state by marriage with Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He first settled in Liaoxi and was known as the Marquis of Xian; his state became a kinsman-realm allied to Wei by marriage.

sentences.zh: 自莫那九世至侯歸豆，為慕容晃所滅。

translations.literal: From Monaj through nine generations to Hou Guidou, they were destroyed by Murong Huang.
translations.idiomatic: From Monaj down through nine generations to Hou Guidou, the line was destroyed by Murong Huang.

sentences.zh: 其子陵仕燕，拜駙馬都尉，封玄菟公。

translations.literal: His son Ling served Yan, was appointed Commandant of Escort Horses, and enfeoffed as Duke of Xuantu.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ling entered the service of Yan, was made Commandant of Escort Horses, and enfeoffed as Duke of Xuantu.

sentences.zh: 及慕容寶敗，歸魏，拜都牧主，賜爵安定侯。

translations.literal: When Murong Bao was defeated, he submitted to Wei, was appointed Chief Pastoral Administrator, and granted the title Marquis of Anding.
translations.idiomatic: When Murong Bao fell, he submitted to Wei, was appointed Chief Pastoral Administrator, and granted the title Marquis of Anding.

sentences.zh: 天興初，魏遷豪傑於代都，陵隨例徙居武川，即為其郡縣人焉。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianxing, Wei relocated the leading families to Dai Commandery; Ling was moved by standard procedure to Wuchuan and became a resident of that county.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Tianxing, Wei moved the great families to the capital at Dai; Ling was relocated in the usual way to Wuchuan and became a man of that district.

sentences.zh: 陵生系，系生韜，韜生皇考肱，並以武略稱。

translations.literal: Ling begat Xi, Xi begat Tao, Tao begat the late Emperor's father Gou; all were known for martial prowess.
translations.idiomatic: Ling fathered Xi, Xi fathered Tao, and Tao fathered the late Emperor's father Gou; all three were famed for military talent.

sentences.zh: 肱任俠有氣幹。

translations.literal: Gou was chivalrous and possessed vigor of spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Gou was a man of chivalry and forceful character.

sentences.zh: 正光末，沃野鎮人破六韓拔陵作亂，其偽署王衛可瑰最盛。

translations.literal: At the end of Zhenguang, the people of Woye Garrison, led by Poliuhan Baling in rebellion; among his self-appointed kings, Wei Kegei was the most powerful.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Zhenguang, the garrison men of Woye rose under Poliuhan Baling; of the rebel kings he appointed, Wei Kegei was the strongest.

sentences.zh: 肱乃糾合鄉里，斬瑰，其眾乃散。

translations.literal: Gou rallied the countryside, beheaded Kegei, and his forces scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Gou gathered the local men, cut down Kegei, and his followers dispersed.

sentences.zh: 後陷鮮于修禮，為定州軍所破，戰沒於陣。

translations.literal: Later he fell in with Xianyu Xiuli; when the Dingzhou army defeated them, he died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Later he joined Xianyu Xiuli; when the Dingzhou army broke them, he fell on the field.

sentences.zh: 武成初，追謚曰德皇帝。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wucheng, he was posthumously given the temple name Emperor De.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Wucheng he was posthumously titled Emperor De.

sentences.zh: 帝，德皇帝之少子也。

translations.literal: The Emperor was the youngest son of Emperor De.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was Emperor De's youngest son.

sentences.zh: 母曰王氏。

translations.literal: His mother was the Lady Wang.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was Lady Wang.

sentences.zh: 初孕五月，夜夢抱子升天，才不至而止。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of her pregnancy, she dreamed of holding a child and ascending to heaven, stopping just short of reaching it.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of her pregnancy she dreamed she was holding a child and climbing toward heaven, stopping only when she had nearly reached the top.

sentences.zh: 寤，以告德皇帝。

translations.literal: Awakening, she told Emperor De.
translations.idiomatic: When she woke, she told Emperor De.

sentences.zh: 德皇帝喜曰：「雖不至天，貴亦極矣。

translations.literal: Emperor De said joyfully: "Though he did not reach heaven, nobility will be at its utmost.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor De said in delight, "Though he did not reach heaven, his rank will be supreme.

sentences.zh: 」帝生而有黑氣如蓋，下覆其身。

translations.literal: " When the Emperor was born, black vapor like a canopy covered him from above.
translations.idiomatic: " At his birth black mist like a canopy descended and shrouded him.

sentences.zh: 及長，身長八尺，方顙廣額，美須髯，發長委地，垂手過膝，背有黑子，宛轉若龍盤之形，面色紫光，人望而敬畏之。

translations.literal: When he grew up, he stood eight feet tall, with a square forehead and broad brow, a fine beard and mustache, hair so long it trailed to the ground, hands that hung below his knees, and a black mark on his back winding like a coiled dragon; his face shone with a purple light, and men who looked upon him felt awe.
translations.idiomatic: Grown to manhood he stood eight feet, with a square forehead and wide brow, a handsome beard, hair falling to the ground, hands reaching past his knees, and a black birthmark on his back coiled like a dragon; his countenance glowed with a purple light, and all who saw him were struck with reverence.

sentences.zh: 少有大度，不事家人生業。

translations.literal: From youth he had great magnanimity and did not pursue the family's livelihood.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a youth he had a broad spirit and took no interest in the household trade.

sentences.zh: 輕財好施，以交結賢士大夫為務。

translations.literal: He was generous and fond of giving, making it his business to befriend worthy gentlemen and scholars.
translations.idiomatic: He gave freely of his wealth and made it his aim to win the friendship of worthy gentlemen and scholars.

sentences.zh: 隨德皇帝在鮮于修禮軍。

translations.literal: He followed Emperor De in Xianyu Xiuli's army.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Emperor De into Xianyu Xiuli's army.

sentences.zh: 及葛榮殺修禮，帝時年十八。

translations.literal: When Ge Rong killed Xiuli, the Emperor was eighteen.
translations.idiomatic: When Ge Rong killed Xiuli, the Emperor was eighteen years old.

sentences.zh: 榮下任將帥，察其無成，謀與諸兄去之。

translations.literal: Ge Rong appointed men as generals and commanders; seeing no prospect of success, the Emperor plotted with his elder brothers to leave.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Rong put his subordinates in command of armies; seeing that he would come to nothing, the Emperor planned with his elder brothers to break away.

sentences.zh: 計未行，會榮滅，因隨爾朱榮遷晉陽。

translations.literal: Before the plan could be carried out, Ge Rong was destroyed; he then followed Erzhu Rong to move to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: Before the plan could be acted on, Ge Rong was destroyed, and he followed Erzhu Rong to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 榮忌帝兄弟雄傑，遂讬以他罪誅帝第三兄洛生。

translations.literal: Rong feared the Emperor and his brothers for their heroic talent; he found another pretext to execute the Emperor's third elder brother Luosheng.
translations.idiomatic: Rong envied the heroic stature of the Emperor and his brothers and, on a fabricated charge, put the Emperor's third elder brother Luosheng to death.

sentences.zh: 帝以家冤自理，辭旨慷慨。

translations.literal: The Emperor pleaded the family's wrong in his own defense, his words impassioned and forthright.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor spoke in his own defense on behalf of the family wrong, his words ardent and unflinching.

sentences.zh: 榮感而免之，益加敬待。

translations.literal: Rong was moved and spared him, treating him with even greater respect.
translations.idiomatic: Rong was touched and released him, showing him even greater regard.

sentences.zh: 始以統軍從榮征討，後以別將從賀拔嶽討北海王顥於洛陽。

translations.literal: At first he served as Army Commander following Rong on campaigns; later as a separate commander he followed Heluo Yue to attack the Prince of Beihai, Yuan Hao, at Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: At first he served as army commander under Rong on campaign; later, as a separate commander, he followed Heluo Yue against the Prince of Beihai, Yuan Hao, at Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 孝莊反正，以功封寧都子。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaozhuang was restored, for his merit he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Ningdu.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaozhuang was restored to the throne, the Emperor was enfeoffed as Viscount of Ningdu for his service.

sentences.zh: 後從嶽入關，平万俟醜奴，行原州事。

translations.literal: Later he followed Yue into the pass, pacified Moqi Chounu, and administered Yuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later he followed Yue through the pass, subdued Moqi Chounu, and acted as administrator of Yuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 時關、隴寇亂，帝撫以恩信，百姓皆喜，曰：「早遇宇文使君，吾等豈從逆亂。

translations.literal: At that time the pass lands and Longxi were in turmoil; the Emperor soothed the people with kindness and trust, and all rejoiced, saying: "Had we met Commissioner Yuwen sooner, we would never have joined the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: In those days Guan and Long were torn by rebellion; the Emperor won the people with kindness and good faith, and they all said with relief, "Had we met Commissioner Yuwen earlier, we would never have gone over to the rebels.

sentences.zh: 」帝嘗從數騎於野，忽聞簫鼓之音，以問從者，皆莫之聞，意獨異之。

translations.literal: " Once, riding with a few horsemen in the open country, he suddenly heard the sound of flutes and drums; he asked his attendants, but none of them heard it, and he alone thought it strange.
translations.idiomatic: " Once, out riding with a handful of men, he suddenly heard flute and drum music; when he asked his companions, none had heard it, and he alone found it strange.

sentences.zh: 普泰二年，爾朱天光東拒齊神武，留弟顯壽鎮長安，召秦州刺史侯莫陳悅東下。

translations.literal: In the second year of Putai, Erzhu Tianguang marched east to oppose the Divine Martial Emperor of Qi, leaving his younger brother Xianshou to hold Chang'an and summoning the Governor of Qinzhou, Houmochen Yue, to come east.
translations.idiomatic: In Putai year two, Erzhu Tianguang marched east against the Divine Martial Emperor of Qi, leaving his brother Xianshou to garrison Chang'an and calling the Governor of Qinzhou, Houmochen Yue, to join him in the east.

sentences.zh: 嶽知天光必敗，欲留悅共圖顯壽，計無所出。

translations.literal: Yue knew Tianguang was bound to fail and wished to keep Yue to join him in a plot against Xianshou, but could find no way to do it.
translations.idiomatic: Yue saw that Tianguang would surely be defeated and wanted to keep Yue with him to take Xianshou, but could think of no means.

sentences.zh: 帝謂嶽曰：「今天光尚近，悅未必貳心；

translations.literal: The Emperor said to Yue: "Tianguang is still near at hand, and Yue may not yet be disloyal at heart;
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor told Yue, "Tianguang is still close, and Yue may not yet be of two minds;

sentences.zh: 若以此事告之，恐其驚懼。

translations.literal: If we tell him of this matter, I fear he will be alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: if we disclose this plan to him, he may panic.

sentences.zh: 然悅雖為主將，不能制物，若先說其眾，必人有留心。

translations.literal: Yet though Yue is the chief commander, he cannot fully control his men; if we speak to the troops first, some among them are sure to hesitate.
translations.idiomatic: Yet though Yue is the commanding general, he cannot fully command his men; if we address the soldiers first, some will surely waver.

sentences.zh: 進失爾朱之期，退恐人情變動；

translations.literal: Advance, and we miss the deadline set by the Erzhu clan; retreat, and I fear the men's hearts will change;
translations.idiomatic: Go forward and we miss the Erzhu deadline; hold back and the troops may turn;

sentences.zh: 若乘此說悅，事無不遂。

translations.literal: if we use this moment to persuade Yue, nothing will fail.
translations.idiomatic: but if we seize this moment to win Yue over, the thing cannot fail.

sentences.zh: 」嶽大喜，即令帝入悅軍說之。

translations.literal: " Yue was greatly pleased and at once sent the Emperor into Yue's camp to persuade him.
translations.idiomatic: " Yue was overjoyed and immediately sent the Emperor into Yue's army to win him over.

sentences.zh: 悅遂與嶽襲長安。

translations.literal: Houmochen Yue then joined Heluo Yue in a surprise attack on Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Houmochen Yue then joined Heluo Yue in a surprise strike on Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 帝輕騎為前鋒，追至華陰，禽顯壽。

translations.literal: The Emperor led the light cavalry as vanguard, pursued to Huayin, and captured Xianshou.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor rode at the head of the light horse, pursued as far as Huayin, and took Xianshou prisoner.

sentences.zh: 及嶽為關西大行臺，以帝為左丞，領嶽府司馬，事無巨細，皆委決焉。

translations.literal: When Yue became Grand Commissioner of the Western Pass, he appointed the Emperor Left Director and put him in charge of the Commissioner's staff as Marshal; matters great and small were all entrusted to his decision.
translations.idiomatic: When Yue became Grand Commissioner of the Western Pass, he made the Emperor Left Director and put him in charge of the commissioner's staff as marshal; every matter, large or small, was left to his judgment.

sentences.zh: 齊神武既除爾朱氏，遂專朝政。

translations.literal: After the Divine Martial Emperor of Qi had eliminated the Erzhu clan, he seized sole control of court affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Divine Martial Emperor of Qi had destroyed the Erzhu clan, he held court power alone.

sentences.zh: 帝請往觀之，至并州。

translations.literal: The Emperor asked leave to go observe him and traveled to Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor asked to go and observe him and went to Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 神武以帝非常人，曰：「此小兒眼目異。

translations.literal: The Divine Martial Emperor saw that the Emperor was no ordinary man and said: "This boy's eyes are strange.
translations.idiomatic: The Divine Martial Emperor saw that the Emperor was no common man and said, "This youth's eyes are unlike any other's.

sentences.zh: 」將留之。

translations.literal: " He intended to detain him.
translations.idiomatic: " He meant to keep him there.

sentences.zh: 帝詭陳忠款，具讬左右，苦求復命，倍道而行。

translations.literal: The Emperor feigned loyal submission, put his case fully before those around him, and begged hard to be sent back on his mission, traveling day and night.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor spoke false words of loyalty, laid his case before the men around him, and pleaded urgently to return on his mission, riding day and night.

sentences.zh: 行一日而神武乃悔，發上驛千里，追帝至關，不及而反。

translations.literal: He had been gone one day when the Divine Martial Emperor repented; he sent post-horses a thousand li in pursuit to the pass, but failed to overtake him and turned back.
translations.idiomatic: One day after he had left, the Divine Martial Emperor regretted his decision and sent relay horses a thousand li in pursuit to the pass, but could not catch him and turned back.

sentences.zh: 帝還，謂嶽曰：「高歡豈人臣邪，逆謀未發者，憚公兄弟耳。

translations.literal: When the Emperor returned, he said to Yue: "Gao Huan is no loyal minister; his rebellion has not yet broken out only because he fears you and your brothers.
translations.idiomatic: On his return the Emperor told Yue, "Gao Huan is no true subject; his treason has not yet surfaced only because he fears you and your brothers.

sentences.zh: 侯莫陳悅本實庸材，亦不為歡忌，但為之備，圖之不難。

translations.literal: Houmochen Yue is by nature a mediocrity and Gao Huan does not fear him either; but if you guard against him and plot his downfall, it will not be hard.
translations.idiomatic: Houmochen Yue is a man of no real talent, and Gao Huan does not fear him either; yet if you take precautions and move against him, it will not be difficult.

sentences.zh: 今費也頭控弦之騎，不下一萬；

translations.literal: Now the Fei Yetou have no fewer than ten thousand bow-bearing horsemen;
translations.idiomatic: The Fei Yetou today field no fewer than ten thousand mounted archers;

sentences.zh: 夏州刺史解拔彌俄突，勝兵三千餘人，及靈州刺史曹泥，並恃僻遠，常懷異望。

translations.literal: the Governor of Xiazhou, Qieba Miyoutu, has more than three thousand seasoned troops; and the Governor of Lingzhou, Cao Ni, together with them all rely on their remote distance and often harbor other designs.
translations.idiomatic: the Governor of Xiazhou, Qieba Miyoutu, has more than three thousand fighting men; and the Governor of Lingzhou, Cao Ni, all of them trusting in their distant posts, often keep rebellious thoughts.

sentences.zh: 河西流人紇豆陵伊利等，戶口富實，未奉朝風。

translations.literal: The exiles of Hexi, such as Hedinling Yili and others, are rich in households and have not yet submitted to the court's influence.
translations.idiomatic: The Hexi exiles, Hedinling Yili and the rest, are wealthy in households and have not yet bowed to the court.

sentences.zh: 今若移軍近隴，扼其要害，示之以威，懷之以德，即可收其士馬，以資吾軍。

translations.literal: If we now shift the army close to Long, hold the key points, show them our might, and win them with kindness, we can at once gather their men and horses to strengthen our forces.
translations.idiomatic: Move the army now to the edge of Long, seize the critical passes, show force and offer kindness, and at once we can take their men and horses to feed our own army.

sentences.zh: 西輯氐、羌，北撫沙塞，還軍長安，匡輔魏室，此桓文之舉也。

translations.literal: Gather the Di and Qiang in the west, pacify the desert frontier in the north, return the army to Chang'an, and support the Wei house: this is an enterprise worthy of Duke Huan and Duke Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Unite the Di and Qiang in the west, soothe the desert marches in the north, bring the army back to Chang'an, and uphold the house of Wei: that is an act in the mold of Duke Huan and Duke Wen.

sentences.zh: 」嶽大悅。

translations.literal: " Yue was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: " Yue was delighted.

sentences.zh: 復遣帝詣闕請事，密陳其狀。

translations.literal: He again sent the Emperor to the capital to report and secretly laid out the plan.
translations.idiomatic: He sent the Emperor again to the capital to petition and secretly set forth the whole design.

sentences.zh: 魏帝納之，加帝武衛將軍，還令報嶽。

translations.literal: The Wei Emperor accepted it, promoted the Emperor to General of Martial Guard, and sent him back to report to Yue.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei Emperor approved, promoted the Emperor to General of Martial Guard, and sent him back to inform Yue.

sentences.zh: 嶽遂引軍西次平涼。

translations.literal: Yue then led his army west and encamped at Pingliang.
translations.idiomatic: Yue then marched west and halted at Pingliang.

sentences.zh: 嶽以夏州鄰接寇賊，欲求良刺史以鎮之，眾皆舉帝。

translations.literal: Because Xiazhou bordered on bandits and raiders, Yue wished to find a capable governor to hold it, and all recommended the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Xiazhou lay against bandit country, and Yue wanted a strong governor to secure it; everyone named the Emperor.

sentences.zh: 嶽曰：「宇文左丞，吾左右手，何可廢也。

translations.literal: Yue said: "Director Yuwen is my right hand; how can I do without him?
translations.idiomatic: Yue said, "Director Yuwen is my right hand; how can I spare him?

sentences.zh: 」沈吟累日，乃從眾議，表帝為夏州刺史。

translations.literal: " He hesitated for many days, then followed the common opinion and memorialized the Emperor as Governor of Xiazhou.
translations.idiomatic: " He brooded for days, then yielded to the general wish and memorialized the Emperor as Governor of Xiazhou.

sentences.zh: 帝至州，伊利望風款附；

translations.literal: When the Emperor reached the province, Yili submitted at the first sight of him;
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor arrived at the province, Yili came over at once;

sentences.zh: 而曹泥猶通使於齊神武。

translations.literal: but Cao Ni still kept up communications with the Divine Martial Emperor of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: but Cao Ni still exchanged envoys with the Divine Martial Emperor of Qi.

sentences.zh: 魏永熙三年正月，賀拔嶽欲討曹泥，遣都督趙貴至夏州與帝謀。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year of Yongxi of Wei, Heluo Yue wished to attack Cao Ni and sent the Commander Zhao Gui to Xiazhou to consult with the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Wei Yongxi year three, Heluo Yue planned to attack Cao Ni and sent Commander Zhao Gui to Xiazhou to consult the Emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「曹泥孤城阻遠，未足為憂。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Cao Ni holds a lone city far away; he is not worth worrying over.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "Cao Ni sits in an isolated city far off; he is no real concern.

sentences.zh: 侯莫陳悅貪而無信，是宜先圖也。

translations.literal: Houmochen Yue is greedy and faithless; he is the one who should be dealt with first.
translations.idiomatic: Houmochen Yue is greedy and untrustworthy; he is the one to strike first.

sentences.zh: 」嶽不聽，遂與悅俱討泥。

translations.literal: " Yue would not listen and went with Yue together to attack Ni.
translations.idiomatic: " Yue would not heed him and marched with Yue together against Ni.

sentences.zh: 二月，至河曲，果為悅所害。

translations.literal: In the second month, when they reached Hequ, Yue was indeed killed by Yue.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, when they reached Hequ, Yue was indeed slain by Yue.

sentences.zh: 眾散還平涼，唯大都督趙貴率部曲收嶽屍還營。

translations.literal: The army scattered back to Pingliang; only the Grand Commander Zhao Gui led his personal troops to recover Yue's body and return to camp.
translations.idiomatic: The army broke and fell back to Pingliang; only Grand Commander Zhao Gui, at the head of his own followers, recovered Yue's body and brought it back to camp.

sentences.zh: 三軍未知所屬，諸將以都督寇洛年最長，推總兵事。

translations.literal: The three armies did not know whom to follow; the generals, because Commander Kou Luonian was the eldest, recommended him to take overall command of military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The three armies had no leader; the generals, judging Commander Kou Luonian the senior man, urged him to take overall command.

sentences.zh: 洛素無雄略，威令不行，乃請避位。

translations.literal: Luo had never possessed heroic strategy, and his authority and orders did not prevail; he therefore asked to step aside.
translations.idiomatic: Luo lacked bold design, and his word carried no weight; he asked to yield command.

sentences.zh: 於是趙貴言於眾，稱帝英姿雄略。

translations.literal: Thereupon Zhao Gui spoke to the assembly, praising the Emperor's heroic bearing and strategic talent.
translations.idiomatic: Then Zhao Gui addressed the assembly and praised the Emperor's heroic mien and strategic mind.

sentences.zh: 若告喪，必來赴難，因而奉之，大事濟矣。

translations.literal: If we announce the mourning, he is sure to come to our aid; if we then raise him up, the great enterprise will succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Announce the death, and he will surely come to our rescue; raise him up, and the great cause will succeed.

sentences.zh: 諸將皆稱善。

translations.literal: All the generals agreed that it was well said.
translations.idiomatic: All the generals approved.

sentences.zh: 乃令赫連達馳至夏州告帝。

translations.literal: They then sent Helianda riding post-haste to Xiazhou to inform the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: They sent Helianda at full speed to Xiazhou to tell the Emperor.

sentences.zh: 士吏咸泣，請留以觀其變。

translations.literal: Officers and clerks all wept and asked him to remain and watch how events would unfold.
translations.idiomatic: The officers and clerks wept and begged him to stay and see how matters would turn.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「難得而易失者時也，不俟終日者機也；

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "What is hard to gain and easy to lose is the moment; what brooks no delay is opportunity;
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "What is hard to win and easy to lose is the moment; what will not wait even a day is the chance;

sentences.zh: 今不早赴，將恐眾心自離。

translations.literal: if we do not go quickly now, I fear the men's hearts will break away on their own.
translations.idiomatic: if we do not go at once, the troops may drift away of their own accord.

sentences.zh: 」都督彌姐元進規應悅，密圖帝。

translations.literal: " Commander Mizhi Yuanjin planned to join Yue and secretly plotted against the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: " Commander Mizhi Yuanjin meant to side with Yue and secretly plotted against the Emperor.

sentences.zh: 事發，斬之。

translations.literal: When the affair came to light, he was beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: When the plot was exposed, he was executed.

sentences.zh: 帝乃率帳下，輕騎馳赴平涼。

translations.literal: The Emperor then led his personal guard and light cavalry in a dash to Pingliang.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor then took his household guard and light horse and raced to Pingliang.

sentences.zh: 時齊神武遣長史侯景招引嶽眾。

translations.literal: At that time the Divine Martial Emperor of Qi had sent Chief Clerk Hou Jing to win over Yue's troops.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Divine Martial Emperor of Qi had sent Chief Clerk Hou Jing to draw off Yue's army.

sentences.zh: 帝至安定，遇之於傳舍。

translations.literal: When the Emperor reached Anding, he met him at the relay station.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor reached Anding, he met him at the post station.

sentences.zh: 吐哺上馬，謂曰：「賀拔公雖死，宇文泰尚存，卿何為也？」

translations.literal: Spitting out his mouthful and mounting his horse, he said to him: "Though Heluo is dead, Yuwen Tai yet lives; what are you about?"
translations.idiomatic: He spat out his food, mounted, and said, "Heluo is dead, but Yuwen Tai still lives; what do you think you are doing?"

sentences.zh: 景失色曰：「我猶箭耳，隨人所射者也。

translations.literal: Jing turned pale and said: "I am but an arrow, shot wherever men aim.
translations.idiomatic: Jing went white and said, "I am only an arrow, loosed wherever men choose to aim.

sentences.zh: 」景於此還。

translations.literal: " At that Jing turned back.
translations.idiomatic: " With that Jing withdrew.

sentences.zh: 帝至平涼，哭嶽甚慟。

translations.literal: When the Emperor reached Pingliang, he wept for Yue with deep grief.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor came to Pingliang, he mourned Yue with bitter grief.

sentences.zh: 將士悲且喜曰：「宇文公至，無所憂矣。

translations.literal: The officers and soldiers were both sorrowful and glad, saying: "Now that Commissioner Yuwen has come, we have nothing left to fear.
translations.idiomatic: The officers and soldiers grieved and rejoiced together, saying, "With Commissioner Yuwen here, we need fear nothing.

sentences.zh: 」齊神武又使景與常侍張華原、義寧太守王基勞帝，帝不受命。

translations.literal: " The Divine Martial Emperor of Qi again sent Jing, together with Regular Attendant Zhang Huayuan and the Administrator of Yining, Wang Ji, to console the Emperor, but the Emperor refused the commission.
translations.idiomatic: " The Divine Martial Emperor of Qi again sent Jing, with Regular Attendant Zhang Huayuan and the Administrator of Yining, Wang Ji, to offer condolences, but the Emperor would not accept the mission.

sentences.zh: 與基有舊，將留之，並欲留景。

translations.literal: He had old ties with Ji and meant to keep him, and wished to keep Jing as well.
translations.idiomatic: He was old friends with Ji and meant to detain him, and he wanted to keep Jing too.

sentences.zh: 並不屈，乃遣之。

translations.literal: They would not submit, so he sent them away.
translations.idiomatic: Neither would submit, and he let them go.

sentences.zh: 時斛斯椿在帝所，曰：「景，人傑也，何故放之？

translations.literal: At that time Husi Chun was with the Emperor and said: "Jing is a man of outstanding talent; why release him?
translations.idiomatic: Husi Chun, who was then at the Emperor's side, said, "Jing is a man of rare ability; why let him go?

sentences.zh: 」帝亦悔，驛追之不及。

translations.literal: " The Emperor also repented and sent post-horses in pursuit, but could not overtake him.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor regretted it too and sent relay horses after him, but could not catch up.

sentences.zh: 基亦逃歸，言帝雄傑，請及其未定滅之。

translations.literal: Ji also fled back and reported that the Emperor was a heroic figure; he asked that they strike before his position was settled and destroy him.
translations.idiomatic: Ji escaped home as well, calling the Emperor a man of heroic stature and urging that they destroy him before his power was fixed.

sentences.zh: 神武曰：「卿不見賀拔、侯莫陳乎，吾當以計拱手取之。

translations.literal: The Divine Martial Emperor said: "Have you not seen Heluo and Houmochen? I shall take him with a stratagem, as though he were handed over to me.
translations.idiomatic: The Divine Martial Emperor said, "Did you not see what became of Heluo and Houmochen? I will take him by design, as if he were delivered into my hands.

sentences.zh: 」及沙苑之敗，神武乃始追悔。

translations.literal: " Only after the defeat at Shawei did the Divine Martial Emperor begin to regret.
translations.idiomatic: " Only after the defeat at Shawei did the Divine Martial Emperor begin to rue his choice.

sentences.zh: 於時魏帝將圖神武。

translations.literal: At that time the Wei Emperor planned to move against the Divine Martial Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Wei Emperor was plotting against the Divine Martial Emperor.

sentences.zh: 聞嶽被害，遣武衛將軍元毗宣旨勞嶽軍，追還洛陽。

translations.literal: When he heard that Yue had been killed, he sent General of Martial Guard Yuan Pi with an imperial message to console Yue's army and summon it back to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Yue had been killed, he sent General of Martial Guard Yuan Pi with an imperial message to comfort Yue's army and recall it to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 毗到平涼，會諸將已推帝。

translations.literal: When Pi reached Pingliang, the generals had already raised the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Pi reached Pingliang just as the generals had already proclaimed the Emperor.

sentences.zh: 侯莫陳悅亦被敕追還。

translations.literal: Houmochen Yue had also received an edict summoning him back.
translations.idiomatic: Houmochen Yue too had been ordered to return.

sentences.zh: 悅既附神武，不肯應召。

translations.literal: Yue had already attached himself to the Divine Martial Emperor and refused the summons.
translations.idiomatic: Yue had already joined the Divine Martial Emperor and would not obey the call.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「悅枉害忠良，復不應詔命，此國之大賊。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Yue wrongfully killed a loyal man and now refuses the imperial command; he is the great villain of the state.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "Yue murdered a loyal man and now defies the imperial summons; he is the state's greatest enemy.

sentences.zh: 」乃令諸軍戒嚴，將討悅。

translations.literal: " He then ordered the armies to stand on alert and prepared to attack Yue.
translations.idiomatic: " He ordered the armies to stand ready and prepared to march against Yue.

sentences.zh: 及毗還，帝表於魏帝，辭以高歡至河東，侯莫陳悅在水洛，首尾受敵，乞少停緩。

translations.literal: When Pi returned, the Emperor memorialized the Wei Emperor, pleading that Gao Huan had reached Hedong and Houmochen Yue held Shuilo, so that they were threatened at both ends, and asking for a brief delay.
translations.idiomatic: When Pi returned, the Emperor memorialized the Wei Emperor, saying that Gao Huan had reached Hedong and Houmochen Yue held Shuilo, leaving them caught between two foes, and begging a short reprieve.

sentences.zh: 帝志在討悅，而未測朝旨；

translations.literal: The Emperor's aim was to attack Yue, but he had not yet gauged the court's intent;
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor meant to strike Yue, but had not yet read the court's mind;

sentences.zh: 且眾未集，假為此辭。

translations.literal: and since the troops were not yet assembled, he offered this excuse.
translations.idiomatic: and with the army not yet gathered, he used this pretext.

sentences.zh: 因與元毗及諸將，刑牲盟誓，同獎王室。

translations.literal: He then joined Yuan Pi and the generals in sacrificing an animal and swearing an oath to support the royal house together.
translations.idiomatic: He then joined Yuan Pi and the generals in sacrificing and swearing to uphold the royal house together.

sentences.zh: 初，賀拔嶽營河曲，軍吏獨行，忽見一翁，謂曰：「賀拔雖據此眾，終無所成。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Heluo Yue encamped at Hequ, a staff officer walking alone suddenly saw an old man who said to him: "Though Heluo holds these troops, in the end he will achieve nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Heluo Yue camped at Hequ, a staff officer walking alone met an old man who said, "Though Heluo commands this army, he will never succeed.

sentences.zh: 當有一宇文家從東北來，後必大盛。

translations.literal: A man of the Yuwen clan will come from the northeast, and afterward will rise to great power.
translations.idiomatic: A man of the Yuwen house will come from the northeast, and afterward his line will flourish.

sentences.zh: 」言訖不見。

translations.literal: " When he had spoken, he vanished.
translations.idiomatic: " With that he disappeared.

sentences.zh: 至是方驗。

translations.literal: Only now was the prophecy fulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: Only now did the prophecy prove true.

sentences.zh: 魏帝因詔帝為大都督，即統賀拔嶽軍。

translations.literal: The Wei Emperor therefore issued an edict appointing the Emperor Grand Commander and putting him in charge of Heluo Yue's army at once.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei Emperor then appointed the Emperor Grand Commander and immediately put him at the head of Heluo Yue's army.

sentences.zh: 帝乃與悅書，責以殺賀拔嶽罪，又喻令歸朝。

translations.literal: The Emperor then wrote to Yue, charging him with the crime of killing Heluo Yue and also urging him to return to court.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor wrote to Yue, accusing him of killing Heluo Yue and urging him to submit to the court.

sentences.zh: 悅乃詐為詔書與秦州刺史万俟普撥，令為己援。

translations.literal: Yue then forged an edict to the Governor of Qinzhou, Moqi Pubo, asking him to come to his aid.
translations.idiomatic: Yue forged an edict to the Governor of Qinzhou, Moqi Pubo, calling on him for support.

sentences.zh: 普撥疑之，封以呈帝，帝表奏之。

translations.literal: Pubo was suspicious, sealed it, and sent it to the Emperor; the Emperor memorialized it to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Pubo doubted it, sealed the letter, and sent it to the Emperor, who reported it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 魏帝因問帝安秦、隴計。

translations.literal: The Wei Emperor then asked the Emperor for his plan to secure Qin and Long.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei Emperor then asked the Emperor how he meant to secure Qin and Long.

sentences.zh: 帝請召悅，授以內官，及處以瓜、涼一籓。

translations.literal: The Emperor asked that Yue be summoned and given an office at court, and that he be assigned the frontier posts of Guazhou and Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor asked that Yue be summoned to court and given an inner office, with Guazhou and Liangzhou set aside for him as a fief.

sentences.zh: 不然，則終致猜虞。

translations.literal: Otherwise suspicion would never end.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise mistrust would never cease.

sentences.zh: 三月，帝進軍至原州，眾軍悉集，諭以討悅意，士卒莫不懷憤。

translations.literal: In the third month the Emperor advanced to Yuanzhou; all the armies assembled, and when he announced his intent to attack Yue, every soldier burned with indignation.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month the Emperor marched to Yuanzhou; the armies gathered, and when he declared his plan to punish Yue, the soldiers seethed with rage.

sentences.zh: 四月，引兵上隴，留兄子遵為都督，鎮原州。

translations.literal: In the fourth month he led his troops up onto Long, leaving his elder brother's son Zun as Commander to garrison Yuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month he led the army onto Long, leaving his nephew Zun as commander to hold Yuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 帝軍令嚴肅，秋毫無犯，百姓大悅。

translations.literal: The Emperor's military discipline was strict; not the slightest thing was taken, and the people were greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor's discipline was severe; not a hair was touched, and the people rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 軍出木峽關，大雪，平地二尺。

translations.literal: When the army passed Muxia Pass, heavy snow fell, two feet deep on level ground.
translations.idiomatic: As the army passed Muxia Pass, snow fell until the flat ground lay two feet deep.

sentences.zh: 帝知悅怯而多猜，乃倍道兼行，出其不意。

translations.literal: The Emperor knew that Yue was timid and full of suspicion; he therefore marched day and night to take him unawares.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing Yue to be cowardly and suspicious, the Emperor forced the march and struck where Yue did not expect him.

sentences.zh: 悅果疑其左右有異志，左右不自安，眾遂離貳。

translations.literal: Yue indeed suspected disloyalty among those around him; his attendants lost confidence, and the army began to split apart.
translations.idiomatic: Yue suspected treachery in his own circle; his men grew uneasy, and the host began to fall apart.

sentences.zh: 聞大軍且至，退保略陽，留一萬餘人據守永洛。

translations.literal: When he heard that the main army was approaching, he withdrew to defend Lueyang, leaving more than ten thousand men to hold Yongluo.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that the main force was near, he fell back to Lueyang and left more than ten thousand men to hold Yongluo.

sentences.zh: 帝至，圍之，城降。

translations.literal: When the Emperor arrived, he besieged it, and the city surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor came up, besieged the city, and it surrendered.

sentences.zh: 帝即輕騎數百趣略陽，以臨悅軍。

translations.literal: The Emperor then rode with a few hundred light horsemen in haste to Lueyang to confront Yue's army.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor then raced ahead with a few hundred light horse to face Yue's camp at Lueyang.

sentences.zh: 其部將皆勸悅退保上邽。

translations.literal: His subordinate commanders all urged Yue to withdraw and hold Shanggui.
translations.idiomatic: Yue's commanders all urged him to fall back and defend Shanggui.

sentences.zh: 時南秦州刺史李弼亦在悅軍，間遣使請為內應。

translations.literal: At that time the Governor of Southern Qinzhou, Li Bi, was also in Yue's army; he secretly sent a messenger offering to act as an inside ally.
translations.idiomatic: Li Bi, Governor of Southern Qinzhou, was then in Yue's camp and secretly sent word offering to work from within.

sentences.zh: 其夜，悅出軍，軍自驚潰，將卒或來降。

translations.literal: That night Yue led his army out; the army panicked and broke on its own, and officers and soldiers came over in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: That night Yue marched out; his own army panicked and collapsed, and officers and men began to surrender.

sentences.zh: 帝縱兵奮擊，大破之。

translations.literal: The Emperor unleashed his troops in fierce attack and routed them completely.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor drove his men in hard and broke them utterly.

sentences.zh: 悅與其子弟及麾下數十騎遁走。

translations.literal: Yue fled with his sons, younger brothers, and several dozen mounted followers.
translations.idiomatic: Yue fled with his sons, brothers, and a few dozen horsemen.

sentences.zh: 帝乃命原州都督導追悅，至牽屯山斬之，傳首洛陽。

translations.literal: The Emperor then ordered the Commander of Yuanzhou, Dao, to pursue Yue; at Qiantun Mountain he was beheaded, and his head was sent to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ordered the Commander of Yuanzhou, Dao, to pursue Yue; at Qiantun Mountain he was cut down, and his head was sent to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 帝至上邽，悅府庫財物山積，皆以賞士卒，毫厘無所取。

translations.literal: When the Emperor reached Shanggui, Yue's treasury stores were piled like hills; he gave it all as reward to the soldiers and took not a fraction for himself.
translations.idiomatic: At Shanggui, Yue's stores stood mountain-high; the Emperor gave it all to the soldiers and kept nothing for himself.

sentences.zh: 左右竊以一銀甕歸，帝知而罪之，即剖賜將士，眾大悅。

translations.literal: An attendant secretly took one silver jar for himself; when the Emperor learned of it he punished him, cut it open, and gave the pieces to the officers and soldiers, and the host rejoiced greatly.
translations.idiomatic: An attendant secretly took a silver jar; the Emperor learned of it, punished the man, broke the jar, and gave the pieces to the troops, and the army was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 齊神武聞關隴克捷，遣使於帝，深相倚結。

translations.literal: When the Divine Martial Emperor of Qi heard that Guan and Long had been taken, he sent envoys to the Emperor to bind themselves closely in alliance.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of the victory in Guan and Long, the Divine Martial Emperor of Qi sent envoys to the Emperor seeking a close alliance.

sentences.zh: 帝拒而不納，封神武書以聞。

translations.literal: The Emperor refused and would not accept; he sealed the Divine Martial Emperor's letter and reported it to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor refused the overture and reported the Divine Martial Emperor's letter, sealed, to the throne.

sentences.zh: 時神武已有異志，故魏帝深仗於帝，仍令帝稍引軍而東。

translations.literal: At that time the Divine Martial Emperor already harbored rebellious intent, so the Wei Emperor relied deeply on the Emperor and ordered him to advance his army gradually eastward.
translations.idiomatic: The Divine Martial Emperor already nursed treasonous designs, and the Wei Emperor leaned heavily on the Emperor, ordering him to draw his army slowly eastward.

sentences.zh: 帝乃令大都督梁禦率步騎五千，將鎮河、渭合口，為圖河東計。

translations.literal: The Emperor then ordered Grand Commander Liang Yu to lead five thousand foot and horse to hold the junction of the He and Wei rivers, planning for an advance into Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ordered Grand Commander Liang Yu to lead five thousand foot and horse to hold the He-Wei confluence, laying plans for Hedong.

sentences.zh: 魏帝進帝侍中、驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、關西大都督、略陽縣公，承制封拜，使持節如故。

translations.literal: The Wei Emperor promoted the Emperor to Palace Attendant, General of Agile Cavalry, Director with the Three Excellencies' Staff, Grand Commander of the Western Pass, Duke of Lueyang County, with authority to appoint and enfeoff by imperial commission, and Bearer of the Staff as before.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei Emperor promoted the Emperor to Palace Attendant, General of Agile Cavalry, Director with the Three Excellencies' Staff, Grand Commander of the Western Pass, Duke of Lueyang County, with commission to appoint and enfeoff by imperial mandate, and Bearer of the Staff unchanged.

sentences.zh: 時魏帝方圖齊神武，又遣征兵。

translations.literal: At that time the Wei Emperor was planning against the Divine Martial Emperor of Qi and again sent orders to raise troops.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei Emperor was then plotting against the Divine Martial Emperor of Qi and again called for troops.

sentences.zh: 帝乃令前秦州刺史駱超為大都督，率輕騎一千赴洛。

translations.literal: The Emperor then appointed the former Governor of Qinzhou, Luo Chao, Grand Commander and sent him with a thousand light horsemen to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor appointed the former Governor of Qinzhou, Luo Chao, Grand Commander and sent him with a thousand light horse to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 魏帝進授帝兼尚書左僕射、關西大行臺，余官如故。

translations.literal: The Wei Emperor further promoted the Emperor to concurrent Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat and Grand Commissioner of the Western Pass; his other offices remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei Emperor further made the Emperor concurrent Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat and Grand Commissioner of the Western Pass; his other titles stood unchanged.

sentences.zh: 帝乃傳檄方鎮曰：蓋聞陰陽遞用，盛衰相襲。

translations.literal: The Emperor then issued a proclamation to the regional commands, saying: I have heard that yin and yang alternate in turn, and prosperity and decline follow one upon another.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor then sent a proclamation to the regional commands, saying: It is said that yin and yang take turns, and rise and fall succeed one another.

sentences.zh: 茍當百六，無聞三五。

translations.literal: Though the age of calamity may come, the age of sage rule is never wholly lost.
translations.idiomatic: Even in the age of ruin, the age of sage kings is never wholly absent.

sentences.zh: 皇家創歷，陶鑄蒼生；

translations.literal: The royal house founded its calendar and molded the common people;
translations.idiomatic: The royal house established its reign and shaped the lives of the people;

sentences.zh: 保安四海，仁育萬物。

translations.literal: it secured the four seas and nourished the myriad beings with benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: it guarded the four seas and nurtured all living things with benevolence.

sentences.zh: 運距孝昌，屯沴屢起，隴、冀騷動，燕、河狼顧。

translations.literal: From the time of Xiaochang, misfortune arose again and again; Long and Ji were shaken, and Yan and He turned wolfish eyes upon the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Since Xiaochang, disaster has struck again and again; Long and Ji have been in turmoil, and Yan and He have looked upon the throne with wolfish eyes.

sentences.zh: 雖靈命重啟，蕩定有期，而乘釁之徒，因翼生羽。

translations.literal: Though Heaven's mandate was renewed and the time of pacification had its term, those who seized the moment grew wings from the chaos.
translations.idiomatic: Though Heaven's mandate was renewed and order had its appointed time, men who seized the moment sprouted wings from the turmoil.

sentences.zh: 賊臣高歡，器識庸下；

translations.literal: The rebel minister Gao Huan is shallow in talent and judgment;
translations.idiomatic: The rebel minister Gao Huan is dull of mind and small of vision;

sentences.zh: 出自輿皂，罕聞禮義。

translations.literal: he came from the lowest ranks and has scarcely heard of ritual and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: born from the carriage-groom's class, he has scarcely known ritual or righteousness.

sentences.zh: 直以一介鷹犬，效力戎行；

translations.literal: He rose only as a single hawk or hound, serving in the army;
translations.idiomatic: He rose only as one hawk or hound, serving on campaign;

sentences.zh: 靦冒恩私，遂階榮寵。

translations.literal: shamelessly accepting private favor, he climbed step by step to glory.
translations.idiomatic: shamelessly accepting private favor, he climbed to rank and favor.

sentences.zh: 不能竭誠盡節，專挾奸回，乃勸爾朱榮行茲篡逆。

translations.literal: He could not exhaust loyalty and devotion, but devoted himself wholly to treachery, and even urged Erzhu Rong to commit usurpation.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to give full loyalty, he gave himself wholly to treachery and even urged Erzhu Rong to usurp the throne.

sentences.zh: 及榮以專政伏誅，世隆以凶黨外叛；

translations.literal: When Rong was executed for monopolizing power, and Shilong rebelled abroad as a vicious partisan;
translations.idiomatic: When Rong was put to death for seizing power, and Shilong rebelled abroad as a villain of his faction;

sentences.zh: 歡苦相敦勉，令取京師。

translations.literal: Huan pressed them hard and urged them to take the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Huan pressed them hard and urged them to seize the capital.

sentences.zh: 又勸吐萬兒復為弒虐，暫立建明，以令天下；

translations.literal: He also urged Tuwan'er to repeat his murderous cruelty, temporarily setting up Jianming to command the realm;
translations.idiomatic: He also urged Tuwan'er to repeat his murderous cruelty, temporarily raising Jianming to rule the realm;

sentences.zh: 假推普泰，欲竊威權。

translations.literal: then falsely promoting Putai, he sought to steal authority for himself.
translations.idiomatic: then falsely promoting Putai, he sought to steal power for himself.

sentences.zh: 並歸廢斥，俱見酷害。

translations.literal: All were cast aside and rejected, and all met cruel destruction.
translations.idiomatic: All were cast aside, and all met cruel ends.

sentences.zh: 於是稱兵河北，假討爾朱；

translations.literal: Thereupon he raised arms in Hebei, falsely claiming to punish the Erzhu;
translations.idiomatic: Then he raised arms in Hebei, falsely claiming to punish the Erzhu;

sentences.zh: 亟通表奏，雲取讒賊。

translations.literal: again and again he sent memorials, saying he would seize the slanderers and villains.
translations.idiomatic: again and again he sent memorials, saying he would seize the slanderers and traitors.

sentences.zh: 既行廢黜，遂將篡弒。

translations.literal: Having carried out deposition, he then moved toward usurpation and regicide.
translations.idiomatic: Having deposed the emperor, he then moved toward usurpation and regicide.

sentences.zh: 以人望未改，恐鼎鑊交及；

translations.literal: Because popular regard had not yet changed, he feared the cauldron and axe might fall upon him;
translations.idiomatic: Because the people's regard had not yet changed, he feared the cauldron and axe might fall on him;

sentences.zh: 乃求宗室，權允人心。

translations.literal: he therefore sought out a member of the imperial clan to satisfy the people for the moment.
translations.idiomatic: he therefore sought a member of the imperial clan to satisfy the people for the moment.

sentences.zh: 天方與魏，必將有主；

translations.literal: Heaven was still with Wei, and there had to be a true sovereign;
translations.idiomatic: Heaven was still with Wei, and a true sovereign had to exist;

sentences.zh: 翊戴聖明，誠非歡力。

translations.literal: to uphold the sage ruler was truly not Huan's doing.
translations.idiomatic: upholding the sage ruler was truly not Huan's work.

sentences.zh: 而歡阻兵安忍，自以為功；

translations.literal: Yet Huan clung to his armies and bore cruelty without remorse, taking all credit for himself;
translations.idiomatic: Yet Huan clung to his armies and bore cruelty without remorse, claiming all credit for himself;

sentences.zh: 廣布腹心，跨州連郡，端揆禁闥，莫非親黨；

translations.literal: he spread his trusted men across provinces and commanderies, and every post at the palace gates was held by his kin;
translations.idiomatic: he spread his trusted men across provinces and commanderies, and every post at the palace gates was held by his kin;

sentences.zh: 皆行貪虐，窫窳生靈。

translations.literal: all practiced greed and cruelty, grinding down the people.
translations.idiomatic: all practiced greed and cruelty, grinding the people down.

sentences.zh: 而舊將名臣，正人直士，橫生瘡磐，動掛網羅。

translations.literal: Old generals and famed ministers, upright men and straight scholars, were wounded as though by plague and constantly caught in his nets.
translations.idiomatic: Old generals and famed ministers, upright men and straight scholars, were wounded as by plague and constantly caught in his nets.

sentences.zh: 故武衛將軍伊琳，清直武毅，禁旅攸屬；

translations.literal: Thus General of Martial Guard Yi Lin, upright, pure, martial, and resolute, belonged to the inner guard;
translations.idiomatic: Thus General of Martial Guard Yi Lin, upright, pure, martial, and resolute, belonged to the inner guard;

sentences.zh: 直閣將軍鮮于康仁，忠亮驍傑，爪牙斯在：歡收而戮之，曾無聞奏。

translations.literal: Direct Attendant General Xianyu Kangren, loyal, bright, bold, and outstanding, stood among his claws and fangs: Huan seized and executed them without ever reporting it to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Direct Attendant General Xianyu Kangren, loyal, bright, bold, and outstanding, stood among his claws and fangs: Huan seized and executed them without ever reporting it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 司空高幹；

translations.literal: Minister of Works Gao Gan;
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Gao Gan;

sentences.zh: 是其黨與，每相影響，謀危社稷。

translations.literal: was his partisan, and they constantly influenced one another, plotting to endanger the state.
translations.idiomatic: was his partisan, and they constantly influenced one another, plotting to endanger the state.

sentences.zh: 但奸誌未從，恐先泄漏，乃密白朝廷，使殺高幹，方哭對其弟，稱天子橫戮。

translations.literal: But because their treacherous design had not yet been carried out, he feared it would leak out first; he therefore secretly reported to the court and had Gao Gan killed, then wept before his brother and called it the emperor's arbitrary execution.
translations.idiomatic: But because their treacherous design had not yet been carried out, he feared it would leak out first; he therefore secretly reported to the court and had Gao Gan killed, then wept before his brother and called it the emperor's arbitrary execution.

sentences.zh: 孫騰、任祥，歡之心膂，並使入居樞近，伺國間隙，知歡逆謀將發，相繼歸逃。

translations.literal: Sun Teng and Ren Xiang, the very core of Huan's counsel, were both sent to hold posts close to the pivot of power to watch for openings in the state; when they learned that Huan's rebellion was about to break out, they fled home one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Teng and Ren Xiang, the very core of Huan's counsel, were both sent to hold posts close to the pivot of power to watch for openings in the state; when they learned that Huan's rebellion was about to break out, they fled home one after another.

sentences.zh: 歡益加撫待，亦無陳白。

translations.literal: Huan treated them with even greater favor and still made no report to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Huan treated them with even greater favor and still made no report to the throne.

sentences.zh: 然歡入洛之始，本有奸謀。

translations.literal: Yet from the time Huan entered Luoyang, he already harbored treacherous designs.
translations.idiomatic: Yet from the time Huan entered Luoyang, he already harbored treacherous designs.

sentences.zh: 令親人蔡俊作牧河、濟，厚相恩贍，為東道主人。

translations.literal: He appointed his kinsman Cai Jun governor of He and Ji, heaping favors upon him to serve as host of the eastern route.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed his kinsman Cai Jun governor of He and Ji, heaping favors upon him to serve as host of the eastern route.

sentences.zh: 故關西大都督清水公賀拔嶽，勛德隆重，興亡攸寄。

translations.literal: Thus the Grand Commander of the Western Pass, Duke of Qingshui, Heluo Yue, whose merit and virtue were weighty and upon whom rise and fall depended.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the Grand Commander of the Western Pass, Duke of Qingshui, Heluo Yue, whose merit and virtue were weighty and upon whom rise and fall depended.

sentences.zh: 歡好亂樂禍，深相忌毒。

translations.literal: Huan loved disorder and rejoiced in calamity, and deeply hated and envied him.
translations.idiomatic: Huan loved disorder and rejoiced in calamity, and deeply hated and envied him.

sentences.zh: 乃與侯莫陳悅，陰圖陷害。

translations.literal: He joined with Houmochen Yue in a secret plot to destroy him.
translations.idiomatic: He joined with Houmochen Yue in a secret plot to destroy him.

sentences.zh: 幕府以受律專征，便即討戮。

translations.literal: The headquarters, having received authority to campaign on its own, at once moved to punish and execute Yue.
translations.idiomatic: The headquarters, having received authority to campaign on its own, at once moved to punish and execute Yue.

sentences.zh: 歡知逆狀已露，稍懷旅拒，遂遣蔡俊拒代；

translations.literal: When Huan learned that his rebellion had been exposed, he grew somewhat defiant and sent Cai Jun to hold Dai;
translations.idiomatic: When Huan learned that his rebellion had been exposed, he grew somewhat defiant and sent Cai Jun to hold Dai;

sentences.zh: 令竇泰佐之。

translations.literal: he had Dou Tai assist him.
translations.idiomatic: he had Dou Tai assist him.

sentences.zh: 又遣侯景等雲向白馬，輔世珍等徑趣石濟，高隆之、及婁昭等屯據壺關，韓軌之徒擁眾蒲阪。

translations.literal: He also sent Hou Jing and others toward Baima in force, Fu Shizhen and others straight toward Shiji, Gao Longzhi and Lou Zhao and others to hold Huguan, and Han Gui and his followers to mass troops at Puyang.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent Hou Jing and others toward Baima in force, Fu Shizhen and others straight toward Shiji, Gao Longzhi and Lou Zhao and others to hold Huguan, and Han Gui and his followers to mass troops at Puyang.

sentences.zh: 於是上書天子，數論得失，訾毀乘輿，威侮朝廷。

translations.literal: Thereupon he memorialized the Son of Heaven, enumerating faults, slandering the imperial carriage, and insulting the court with overbearing force.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he memorialized the Son of Heaven, enumerating faults, slandering the imperial carriage, and insulting the court with overbearing force.

sentences.zh: 藉此微庸，冀茲大寶；

translations.literal: On the strength of these petty services, he hoped for the great treasure;
translations.idiomatic: On the strength of these petty services, he hoped for the great treasure;

sentences.zh: 溪壑可盈，禍心不測。

translations.literal: ravines and gullies may be filled, but his treacherous heart cannot be measured.
translations.idiomatic: ravines and gullies may be filled, but his treacherous heart cannot be measured.

sentences.zh: 或言徑赴荊、楚，開疆於外；

translations.literal: Some say he will march straight to Jing and Chu and open new territory abroad;
translations.idiomatic: Some say he will march straight to Jing and Chu and open new territory abroad;

sentences.zh: 或言分詣伊、洛，取彼讒人；

translations.literal: Some say he will divide his forces and march on Yi and Luo to seize the slanderers there;
translations.idiomatic: Some say he will divide his forces and march on Yi and Luo to seize the slanderers there;

sentences.zh: 或言欲來入關，與幕府決戰。

translations.literal: Some say he intends to enter the pass and fight a decisive battle with the headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Some say he means to enter the pass and fight a decisive battle with the headquarters.

sentences.zh: 今聖明禦運，天下清夷；

translations.literal: Now the sage ruler holds the throne, and the realm is clear and tranquil;
translations.idiomatic: Now the sage ruler holds the throne, and the realm is clear and tranquil;

sentences.zh: 百僚師師，四隩來暨；

translations.literal: the hundred officials serve in order, and the four corners of the earth come to pay homage;
translations.idiomatic: the hundred officials serve in order, and the four corners of the earth come to pay homage;

sentences.zh: 人盡忠良，誰為君側？

translations.literal: every man is loyal and good; who then stands at the ruler's side as villain?
translations.idiomatic: every man is loyal and good; who then stands at the ruler's side as villain?

sentences.zh: 而歡威福自己，生是亂階；

translations.literal: Yet Huan wields fortune and authority for himself and is himself the source of disorder;
translations.idiomatic: Yet Huan wields fortune and authority for himself and is himself the source of disorder;

sentences.zh: 緝構南箕，指鹿為馬；

translations.literal: he weaves slander like the Southern Dipper and calls a deer a horse;
translations.idiomatic: he weaves slander like the Southern Dipper and calls a deer a horse;

sentences.zh: 包藏凶逆，伺我神器。

translations.literal: he harbors treachery and rebellion and watches for his chance at the imperial regalia.
translations.idiomatic: he harbors treachery and rebellion and watches for his chance at the imperial regalia.

sentences.zh: 是而可忍，孰不可容。

translations.literal: If this can be borne, what cannot be endured?
translations.idiomatic: If this can be borne, what cannot be endured?

sentences.zh: 幕府折沖宇宙，親當受脤；

translations.literal: The headquarters checks the enemy throughout the realm and has personally received the sacrificial flesh;
translations.idiomatic: The headquarters checks the enemy throughout the realm and has personally received the sacrificial flesh;

sentences.zh: 銳師百萬，彀騎千群；

translations.literal: sharp troops number in the millions, and armored horsemen stand in thousands of squadrons;
translations.idiomatic: sharp troops number in the millions, and armored horsemen stand in thousands of squadrons;

sentences.zh: 裹糧坐甲，唯敵是俟；

translations.literal: with provisions wrapped and armor donned, we wait only for the enemy;
translations.idiomatic: with provisions wrapped and armor donned, we wait only for the enemy;

sentences.zh: 義之所在，糜軀匪吝。

translations.literal: where righteousness lies, we do not grudge the shattering of our bodies.
translations.idiomatic: where righteousness lies, we do not grudge the shattering of our bodies.

sentences.zh: 頻有詔書，班告天下；

translations.literal: Edicts have repeatedly been issued and proclaimed throughout the realm;
translations.idiomatic: Edicts have repeatedly been issued and proclaimed throughout the realm;

sentences.zh: 稱歡逆亂，征兵致伐。

translations.literal: declaring Huan's rebellion and calling for troops to march against him.
translations.idiomatic: declaring Huan's rebellion and calling for troops to march against him.

sentences.zh: 今便分命將帥，應機進討。

translations.literal: Now at once we assign commanders and generals to advance and attack as occasion demands.
translations.idiomatic: Now at once we assign commanders and generals to advance and attack as occasion demands.

sentences.zh: 或趣其要害，或襲其窟穴，電繞蛇擊，霧合星羅。

translations.literal: Some will strike his vital points, some will raid his lairs; like lightning circling and serpents striking, like mist gathering and stars arrayed.
translations.idiomatic: Some will strike his vital points, some will raid his lairs; like lightning circling and serpents striking, like mist gathering and stars arrayed.

sentences.zh: 而歡違負天地，毒被人鬼；

translations.literal: Yet Huan has betrayed Heaven and Earth, and his poison afflicts both men and spirits;
translations.idiomatic: Yet Huan has betrayed Heaven and Earth, and his poison afflicts both men and spirits;

sentences.zh: 乘此掃蕩，易同俯拾。

translations.literal: taking advantage of this moment to sweep him away will be as easy as picking up what lies at one's feet.
translations.idiomatic: taking advantage of this moment to sweep him away will be as easy as picking up what lies at one's feet.

sentences.zh: 歡若度河，稍逼宮廟，則分命諸將，直取并州。

translations.literal: If Huan crosses the river and presses close upon the palace and temples, then we shall assign the generals to march straight on Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: If Huan crosses the river and presses close upon the palace and temples, then we shall assign the generals to march straight on Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 幕府躬自東轅，電赴伊、洛。

translations.literal: The headquarters will itself turn the chariot eastward and fly to Yi and Luo.
translations.idiomatic: The headquarters will itself turn the chariot eastward and fly to Yi and Luo.

sentences.zh: 若固其巢穴，未敢發動；

translations.literal: If he holds fast in his nest and dares not stir;
translations.idiomatic: If he holds fast in his nest and dares not stir;

sentences.zh: 亦命群帥，百道俱前，轘裂賊臣，以謝天下。

translations.literal: we shall also command the commanders to advance on a hundred routes, tear the rebel minister limb from limb, and settle accounts with the realm.
translations.idiomatic: we shall also command the commanders to advance on a hundred routes, tear the rebel minister limb from limb, and settle accounts with the realm.

sentences.zh: 其州鎮郡縣，率土黎人，或州鄉冠冕，或勛庸世濟，並宜舍逆歸順，立效軍門。

translations.literal: In every province, garrison, commandery, and county, and among all the common people under heaven, whether men of local eminence or families of long-standing merit, all should abandon rebellion and return to loyalty, and prove their service at the army gate.
translations.idiomatic: In every province, garrison, commandery, and county, and among all the common people under heaven, whether men of local eminence or families of long-standing merit, all should abandon rebellion and return to loyalty, and prove their service at the army gate.

sentences.zh: 封賞之科，已有別格；

translations.literal: The standards for enfeoffment and reward already stand in separate regulations;
translations.idiomatic: The standards for enfeoffment and reward already stand in separate regulations;

sentences.zh: 凡百君子，可不勉哉。

translations.literal: all you gentlemen should exert yourselves without fail.
translations.idiomatic: all you gentlemen should exert yourselves without fail.

sentences.zh: 帝謂諸軍曰：「高歡雖智不足而詐有餘，今聲言欲西，其意在入洛。

translations.literal: The Emperor said to the armies: "Though Gao Huan lacks wisdom, he has treachery to spare; now he declares he will go west, but his intent is to enter Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor told the armies, "Though Gao Huan lacks wisdom, he has treachery to spare; now he declares he will go west, but his intent is to enter Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 吾欲令寇洛率馬步萬餘，自涇州東引；

translations.literal: I wish to have Kou Luo lead more than ten thousand foot and horse eastward from Jingzhou;
translations.idiomatic: I wish to have Kou Luo lead more than ten thousand foot and horse eastward from Jingzhou;

sentences.zh: 王羆率甲士一萬，先據華州。

translations.literal: Wang Pi will lead ten thousand armored soldiers and seize Huazhou first.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Pi will lead ten thousand armored soldiers and seize Huazhou first.

sentences.zh: 歡若西來，王羆足得抗拒；

translations.literal: If Huan comes west, Wang Pi will be fully able to hold him off;
translations.idiomatic: If Huan comes west, Wang Pi will be fully able to hold him off;

sentences.zh: 如其入洛，寇洛即襲汾、晉。

translations.literal: if he enters Luoyang, Kou Luo will strike Fen and Jin.
translations.idiomatic: if he enters Luoyang, Kou Luo will strike Fen and Jin.

sentences.zh: 吾便速駕，直赴京邑，使其進有內顧之憂，退有被躡之勢。

translations.literal: I shall then ride swiftly and go straight to the capital, so that advancing he will have worry for his rear, and retreating he will face the threat of pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: I shall then ride swiftly and go straight to the capital, so that advancing he will have worry for his rear, and retreating he will face the threat of pursuit.

sentences.zh: 一舉大定，此為上策。

translations.literal: One stroke and all will be settled; this is the best plan.
translations.idiomatic: One stroke and all will be settled; this is the best plan.

sentences.zh: 」眾咸稱善。

translations.literal: " All agreed that it was well said.
translations.idiomatic: " All agreed that it was well said.

sentences.zh: 七月，帝帥眾發自高平，前軍至於弘農。

translations.literal: In the seventh month the Emperor led his troops out from Gaoping; the vanguard reached Hongnong.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month the Emperor led his troops out from Gaoping; the vanguard reached Hongnong.

sentences.zh: 而齊神武稍逼京師，魏帝親總六軍屯河橋，令左衛元斌之、領軍斛斯椿鎮武牢。

translations.literal: Meanwhile the Divine Martial Emperor of Qi pressed gradually toward the capital; the Wei Emperor personally commanded the Six Armies and encamped at Heqiao, ordering Left Guard Yuan Binzhi and Army Director Husi Chun to hold Wulao.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile the Divine Martial Emperor of Qi pressed gradually toward the capital; the Wei Emperor personally commanded the Six Armies and encamped at Heqiao, ordering Left Guard Yuan Binzhi and Army Director Husi Chun to hold Wulao.

sentences.zh: 帝謂左右曰：「高歡數日行八九百里，曉兵者所忌，正須乘便擊之。

translations.literal: The Emperor said to those around him: "Gao Huan travels eight or nine hundred li in a few days; this is what a man who understands warfare must avoid, and we should seize the moment to strike him.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said to those around him, "Gao Huan travels eight or nine hundred li in a few days; this is what a man who understands warfare must avoid, and we should seize the moment to strike him.

sentences.zh: 而主上以萬乘之重，不能度河決戰，方緣津據守。

translations.literal: Yet the sovereign, with the weight of the imperial chariot upon him, will not cross the river for a decisive battle and instead holds the fords along the bank.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the sovereign, with the weight of the imperial chariot upon him, will not cross the river for a decisive battle and instead holds the fords along the bank.

sentences.zh: 且長河萬里，捍禦為難，一處得度，大事去矣。

translations.literal: The Long River runs ten thousand li; to defend it is hard, and if the enemy finds one crossing, the great enterprise is lost.
translations.idiomatic: The Long River runs ten thousand li; to defend it is hard, and if the enemy finds one crossing, the great enterprise is lost.

sentences.zh: 」即以大都督趙貴為別道行臺，自蒲阪濟，趣并州。

translations.literal: " He then appointed Grand Commander Zhao Gui Separate Commissioner and had him cross at Puyang, pressing toward Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: " He then appointed Grand Commander Zhao Gui Separate Commissioner and had him cross at Puyang, pressing toward Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 遣大都督李賢將精騎一千赴洛陽。

translations.literal: He sent Grand Commander Li Xian with a thousand elite horsemen to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Grand Commander Li Xian with a thousand elite horsemen to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 會斌之與斛斯椿爭權，鎮防不守，魏帝遂輕騎入關。

translations.literal: Binzhi and Husi Chun contended for power; the garrison defenses were not held, and the Wei Emperor therefore entered the pass with a light escort.
translations.idiomatic: Binzhi and Husi Chun contended for power; the garrison defenses were not held, and the Wei Emperor therefore entered the pass with a light escort.

sentences.zh: 帝備儀衛奉迎，謁見於陽驛，免冠流涕謝罪。

translations.literal: The Emperor prepared ceremonial guards to welcome him, met him at Yangyi, removed his cap, and wept as he asked forgiveness.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor prepared ceremonial guards to welcome him, met him at Yangyi, removed his cap, and wept as he asked forgiveness.

sentences.zh: 乃奉魏帝都長安。

translations.literal: He then escorted the Wei Emperor to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: He then escorted the Wei Emperor to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 披草萊，立朝廷，軍國之政，咸取決於帝。

translations.literal: Clearing the wild growth, he established a court, and military and state affairs were all decided by the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Clearing the wild growth, he established a court, and military and state affairs were all decided by the Emperor.

sentences.zh: 仍加授大將軍、雍州刺史，兼尚書令，進封略陽郡公。

translations.literal: He was further promoted to Grand General and Governor of Yongzhou, made concurrent Director of the Imperial Secretariat, and advanced to Duke of Lueyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was further promoted to Grand General and Governor of Yongzhou, made concurrent Director of the Imperial Secretariat, and advanced to Duke of Lueyang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 別置二尚書，隨機處分。

translations.literal: Two additional Directors of the Imperial Secretariat were established to handle matters as occasion required.
translations.idiomatic: Two additional Directors of the Imperial Secretariat were established to handle matters as occasion required.

sentences.zh: 解尚書僕射，余如故。

translations.literal: He was relieved of Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat; his other offices remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was relieved of Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat; his other offices remained as before.

sentences.zh: 初，魏帝在洛陽，許以馮翊長公主配帝，未及結納而魏帝西遷。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Wei Emperor was at Luoyang, he had promised to give the Princess of Fengyi in marriage to the Emperor, but before the betrothal could be completed the Wei Emperor moved west.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the Wei Emperor was at Luoyang, he had promised to give the Princess of Fengyi in marriage to the Emperor, but before the betrothal could be completed the Wei Emperor moved west.

sentences.zh: 至是詔帝尚之，拜附馬都尉。

translations.literal: At this time an edict ordered the Emperor to marry her, and he was appointed Commandant of Escort Horses.
translations.idiomatic: At this time an edict ordered the Emperor to marry her, and he was appointed Commandant of Escort Horses.

sentences.zh: 八月，齊神武襲陷潼關，侵華陰。

translations.literal: In the eighth month the Divine Martial Emperor of Qi struck and took Tong Pass and invaded Huayin.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month the Divine Martial Emperor of Qi struck and took Tong Pass and invaded Huayin.

sentences.zh: 帝率諸軍屯霸上以待之。

translations.literal: The Emperor led the armies to encamp at Bashang and wait for him.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor led the armies to encamp at Bashang and wait for him.

sentences.zh: 神武留其將薛瑾守關而退。

translations.literal: The Divine Martial Emperor left his general Xue Jin to hold the pass and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The Divine Martial Emperor left his general Xue Jin to hold the pass and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 帝乃進軍斬瑾，虜其卒七千。

translations.literal: The Emperor then advanced, beheaded Jin, and captured seven thousand of his soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor then advanced, beheaded Jin, and captured seven thousand of his soldiers.

sentences.zh: 還長安，進位丞相。

translations.literal: Returning to Chang'an, he was promoted to Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Returning to Chang'an, he was promoted to Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 十一月，遣儀同李虎與李弼、趙貴等討曹泥於靈州，虎引河灌之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month he sent Commissioner of Protocol Li Hu with Li Bi, Zhao Gui, and others to attack Cao Ni at Lingzhou; Hu diverted the river to flood the city.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he sent Commissioner of Protocol Li Hu with Li Bi, Zhao Gui, and others to attack Cao Ni at Lingzhou; Hu diverted the river to flood the city.

sentences.zh: 明年，泥降，遷其豪帥於咸陽。

translations.literal: The next year Ni surrendered, and their chieftains were moved to Xianyang.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Ni surrendered, and their chieftains were moved to Xianyang.

sentences.zh: 十二月，魏孝武帝崩，帝與群公定冊，尊立魏南陽王寶炬為嗣，是為文帝。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Emperor Xiaowu of Wei died; the Emperor joined the high officials in fixing the succession and raised the Prince of Nanyang, Yuan Baoju, as heir; this was Emperor Wen.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Emperor Xiaowu of Wei died; the Emperor joined the high officials in fixing the succession and raised the Prince of Nanyang, Yuan Baoju, as heir; this was Emperor Wen.

sentences.zh: 大統元年正月己酉，魏帝進帝都督中外諸軍、錄尚書事、大行臺，改封安定郡王。

translations.literal: On the day jiyou of the first month of the first year of Datong, the Wei Emperor promoted the Emperor to Director of All Armies at Home and Abroad, Recorder of Affairs of the Imperial Secretariat, and Grand Commissioner, and changed his enfeoffment to Prince of Anding Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jiyou of the first month of Datong year one, the Wei Emperor promoted the Emperor to Director of All Armies at Home and Abroad, Recorder of Affairs of the Imperial Secretariat, and Grand Commissioner, and changed his enfeoffment to Prince of Anding Commandery.

sentences.zh: 帝固讓王及錄尚書。

translations.literal: The Emperor firmly declined the princely title and the post of Recorder of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor firmly declined the princely title and the post of Recorder of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 魏帝許之，乃改封安定郡公。

translations.literal: The Wei Emperor consented, and he was therefore changed to Duke of Anding Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei Emperor consented, and he was therefore changed to Duke of Anding Commandery.

sentences.zh: 東魏將同司馬子如寇潼關，帝軍霸上。

translations.literal: The Eastern Wei general Sima Ziru raided Tong Pass; the Emperor's army was at Bashang.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Wei general Sima Ziru raided Tong Pass; the Emperor's army was at Bashang.

sentences.zh: 子如乃回軍自蒲津寇華州，刺史王羆擊走之。

translations.literal: Ziru then turned his army back, crossed at Pujin, and raided Huazhou; the Governor Wang Pi drove him off.
translations.idiomatic: Ziru then turned his army back, crossed at Pujin, and raided Huazhou; the Governor Wang Pi drove him off.

sentences.zh: 三月，帝命有司為二十四條新制，奏行之。

translations.literal: In the third month the Emperor ordered the relevant offices to draft twenty-four new regulations and memorialized them for enactment.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month the Emperor ordered the relevant offices to draft twenty-four new regulations and memorialized them for enactment.

sentences.zh: 二年五月，秦州刺史、建忠王万俟普撥率所部入東魏。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the second year, the Governor of Qinzhou, Prince of Jianzhong, Moqi Pubo, led his followers into Eastern Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the second year, the Governor of Qinzhou, Prince of Jianzhong, Moqi Pubo, led his followers into Eastern Wei.

sentences.zh: 帝輕騎追之，至河北千餘里，不及而還。

translations.literal: The Emperor pursued with light cavalry more than a thousand li north of the river, but could not overtake him and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor pursued with light cavalry more than a thousand li north of the river, but could not overtake him and returned.

sentences.zh: 三年正月，東魏寇龍門，屯軍蒲阪，造三道浮橋度河。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year, Eastern Wei raided Longmen, encamped at Puyang, and built three pontoon bridges to cross the river.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the third year, Eastern Wei raided Longmen, encamped at Puyang, and built three pontoon bridges to cross the river.

sentences.zh: 又遣其將竇泰趣潼關，高昂圍洛州。

translations.literal: They also sent their general Dou Tai toward Tong Pass and Gao Ao to besiege Luozhou.
translations.idiomatic: They also sent their general Dou Tai toward Tong Pass and Gao Ao to besiege Luozhou.

sentences.zh: 帝出軍廣陽，召諸將謂曰：「賊掎吾三面，又造橋，示欲必度，是欲綴吾軍，使竇泰得西入耳。

translations.literal: The Emperor led his army out to Guangyang and summoned the generals, saying: "The enemy has seized three sides of us and built bridges, showing that they mean to cross for certain; they mean to pin our army so that Dou Tai can slip west.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor led his army out to Guangyang and summoned the generals, saying, "The enemy has seized three sides of us and built bridges, showing that they mean to cross for certain; they mean to pin our army so that Dou Tai can slip west.

sentences.zh: 且歡起兵以來，泰每先驅，下多銳卒，屢勝而驕。

translations.literal: Moreover, since Huan raised his army, Tai has always led the van; his men below are mostly sharp troops, and repeated victory has made them arrogant.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, since Huan raised his army, Tai has always led the van; his men below are mostly sharp troops, and repeated victory has made them arrogant.

sentences.zh: 今襲之必克。

translations.literal: If we strike them now, we are sure to overcome them.
translations.idiomatic: If we strike them now, we are sure to overcome them.

sentences.zh: 克泰，則歡不戰而走矣。

translations.literal: If we overcome Tai, Huan will flee without fighting.
