translations.idiomatic: If we overcome Tai, Huan will flee without fighting.

sentences.zh: 」諸將咸曰：「賊在近，舍而襲遠；

translations.literal: " All the generals said: "The enemy is near; to abandon them and strike far away;
translations.idiomatic: " All the generals said, "The enemy is near; to abandon them and strike far away;

sentences.zh: 若差跌，悔何及也。

translations.literal: if we stumble, what regret will there be?
translations.idiomatic: if we stumble, what regret will there be?

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「歡前再襲潼關，吾軍不過霸上。

translations.literal: " The Emperor said: "When Huan twice before raided Tong Pass, our army did not go beyond Bashang.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor said, "When Huan twice before raided Tong Pass, our army did not go beyond Bashang.

sentences.zh: 今者大來，謂吾但自守耳。

translations.literal: Now that he comes in force, he thinks we will only defend ourselves.
translations.idiomatic: Now that he comes in force, he thinks we will only defend ourselves.

sentences.zh: 又狃於得志，有輕我之心。

translations.literal: He is also accustomed to success and holds us in contempt.
translations.idiomatic: He is also accustomed to success and holds us in contempt.

sentences.zh: 乘此擊之，何往不克。

translations.literal: Strike at this moment, and where will we not prevail?
translations.idiomatic: Strike at this moment, and where will we not prevail?

sentences.zh: 賊雖造橋，未能徑度，比五日中，吾取泰必矣。

translations.literal: Though the enemy has built bridges, they cannot cross directly; within five days I shall take Tai for certain.
translations.idiomatic: Though the enemy has built bridges, they cannot cross directly; within five days I shall take Tai for certain.

sentences.zh: 」庚戌，帝還長安，聲言欲向隴右。

translations.literal: " On the day gengxu the Emperor returned to Chang'an, declaring publicly that he intended to go toward Longyou.
translations.idiomatic: " On the day gengxu the Emperor returned to Chang'an, declaring publicly that he intended to go toward Longyou.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，謁魏帝而潛軍至小關。

translations.literal: On the day xinhai he paid his respects to the Wei Emperor, then secretly led the army to Xiaoguan.
translations.idiomatic: On the day xinhai he paid his respects to the Wei Emperor, then secretly led the army to Xiaoguan.

sentences.zh: 竇泰卒聞軍至，陳未成，帝擊之。

translations.literal: Dou Tai's soldiers heard the army had arrived before their formation was complete; the Emperor attacked them.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Tai's soldiers heard the army had arrived before their formation was complete; the Emperor attacked them.

sentences.zh: 盡俘其眾，斬泰，傳首長安。

translations.literal: He captured the whole host, beheaded Tai, and sent his head to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: He captured the whole host, beheaded Tai, and sent his head to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 高昂聞之，焚輜重而走。

translations.literal: When Gao Ao heard of it, he burned his baggage train and fled.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Ao heard of it, he burned his baggage train and fled.

sentences.zh: 齊神武亦撤橋而退。

translations.literal: The Divine Martial Emperor of Qi also dismantled his bridges and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The Divine Martial Emperor of Qi also dismantled his bridges and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 帝乃還。

translations.literal: The Emperor then returned.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor then returned.

sentences.zh: 六月，帝請罷行臺，魏帝復申前命，授帝錄尚書事，固讓乃止。

translations.literal: In the sixth month the Emperor asked to abolish the Grand Commission; the Wei Emperor again repeated the earlier appointment and granted him Recorder of Affairs of the Imperial Secretariat, but he firmly declined and the matter stopped.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month the Emperor asked to abolish the Grand Commission; the Wei Emperor again repeated the earlier appointment and granted him Recorder of Affairs of the Imperial Secretariat, but he firmly declined and the matter stopped.

sentences.zh: 八月丁丑，帝率李弼、獨孤信、梁禦、趙貴、於謹、若干惠、怡峰、劉亮、王德、侯莫陳崇、李遠、達奚武等十二將東伐，至潼關。

translations.literal: On the day dingchou of the eighth month the Emperor led Li Bi, Dugu Xin, Liang Yu, Zhao Gui, Yu Jin, Ruogan Hui, Yi Feng, Liu Liang, Wang De, Houmochen Chong, Li Yuan, Daxi Wu, and twelve other generals east on campaign to Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: On the day dingchou of the eighth month the Emperor led Li Bi, Dugu Xin, Liang Yu, Zhao Gui, Yu Jin, Ruogan Hui, Yi Feng, Liu Liang, Wang De, Houmochen Chong, Li Yuan, Daxi Wu, and twelve other generals east on campaign to Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 帝乃誓於師曰：「與爾有眾，奉天威，誅暴亂。

translations.literal: The Emperor then swore an oath before the army, saying: "With you I have this host; by Heaven's majesty we shall punish violence and disorder.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor then swore an oath before the army, saying, "With you I have this host; by Heaven's majesty we shall punish violence and disorder.

sentences.zh: 惟爾眾士，整爾甲兵，戒爾戎事，無貪財以輕敵，無暴人以作威。

translations.literal: You officers and soldiers, put your armor in order, guard your military duties, do not covet wealth and so treat the enemy lightly, and do not brutalize the people to make a show of might.
translations.idiomatic: You officers and soldiers, put your armor in order, guard your military duties, do not covet wealth and so treat the enemy lightly, and do not brutalize the people to make a show of might.

sentences.zh: 用命則有賞，不用命則有戮，爾眾士其勉之。

translations.literal: Obey orders and there will be reward; disobey orders and there will be execution; you officers and soldiers, exert yourselves.
translations.idiomatic: Obey orders and there will be reward; disobey orders and there will be execution; you officers and soldiers, exert yourselves.

sentences.zh: 」乃遣於謹先徇地至盤豆，拔之。

translations.literal: " He then sent Yu Jin ahead to advance through the territory as far as Pandou and took it.
translations.idiomatic: " He then sent Yu Jin ahead to advance through the territory as far as Pandou and took it.

sentences.zh: 獲東魏將高叔禮，送於長安。

translations.literal: They captured the Eastern Wei general Gao Shuli and sent him to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: They captured the Eastern Wei general Gao Shuli and sent him to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 戊子，至弘農，攻之，城潰。

translations.literal: On the day wuzi they reached Hongnong and attacked it; the city collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: On the day wuzi they reached Hongnong and attacked it; the city collapsed.

sentences.zh: 禽東魏陜州刺史李徽伯，虜其戰士八千。

translations.literal: They captured the Eastern Wei Governor of Shaanzhou, Li Huibo, and took eight thousand of his fighting men.
translations.idiomatic: They captured the Eastern Wei Governor of Shaanzhou, Li Huibo, and took eight thousand of his fighting men.

sentences.zh: 守將高千走度河，命賀拔勝追禽之，並送長安。

translations.literal: The defending general Gao Qian fled across the river; the Emperor ordered Heluo Sheng to pursue and capture him, and both were sent to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: The defending general Gao Qian fled across the river; the Emperor ordered Heluo Sheng to pursue and capture him, and both were sent to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 於是宜陽、邵郡皆歸附。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yiyang and Shao Commandery all submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Yiyang and Shao Commandery all submitted.

sentences.zh: 先是河南豪傑應東魏者，皆降。

translations.literal: Earlier, the leading men south of the river who had sided with Eastern Wei all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the leading men south of the river who had sided with Eastern Wei all surrendered.

sentences.zh: 齊神武懼，率眾下蒲阪，將自后土濟。

translations.literal: The Divine Martial Emperor of Qi was afraid and led his troops down to Puyang, intending to cross from Houtu.
translations.idiomatic: The Divine Martial Emperor of Qi was afraid and led his troops down to Puyang, intending to cross from Houtu.

sentences.zh: 遣其將高昂以三萬人出河南。

translations.literal: He sent his general Gao Ao with thirty thousand men out into Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He sent his general Gao Ao with thirty thousand men out into Henan.

sentences.zh: 是歲，關中饑，帝館谷於弘農五十餘日。

translations.literal: That year famine struck Guanzhong; the Emperor stored grain at Hongnong for more than fifty days.
translations.idiomatic: That year Guanzhong suffered famine, and the Emperor kept grain at Hongnong for more than fifty days.

sentences.zh: 時軍士不滿萬人，聞神武將度，乃還。

translations.literal: At that time the army numbered fewer than ten thousand men; hearing that the Divine Martial Emperor was about to cross, they returned.
translations.idiomatic: The army then numbered fewer than ten thousand; hearing the Divine Martial Emperor meant to cross, they turned back.

sentences.zh: 神武遂度河，逼華州。

translations.literal: The Divine Martial Emperor then crossed the river and pressed on Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Divine Martial Emperor crossed the river and pressed Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 刺史王羆嚴守，乃涉洛，軍於許原西。

translations.literal: The Governor Wang Pi held the city strictly; the Divine Martial Emperor then crossed the Luo and encamped west of Xuyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Wang Pi held firm, so the Divine Martial Emperor crossed the Luo and encamped west of Xuyuan.

sentences.zh: 帝至渭南，征諸州兵，未會。

translations.literal: The Emperor reached Weinan and called up troops from the provinces, but they had not yet assembled.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor reached Weinan and called up provincial troops, but they had not yet gathered.

sentences.zh: 將擊之，諸將以眾寡不敵，請且待歡更西以觀之。

translations.literal: He was about to attack when the generals, judging their numbers too few against the enemy, asked to wait until Huan moved further west and observe.
translations.idiomatic: He meant to attack, but the generals, seeing they were outnumbered, asked to wait until Huan moved further west.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「歡若至咸陽，人情轉騷擾。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "If Huan reaches Xianyang, the people's hearts will turn to turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "If Huan reaches Xianyang, the people will fall into panic.

sentences.zh: 今及其新至，可擊之。

translations.literal: Now, while he has just arrived, we can strike him.
translations.idiomatic: Strike him now, while he has only just arrived.

sentences.zh: 」即造浮橋於渭，令軍士賫三日糧，輕騎度渭，輜重自渭南，夾渭而西。

translations.literal: " He at once built pontoon bridges on the Wei, ordered the soldiers to carry three days' rations, crossed the Wei with light cavalry, and had the baggage train come from Weinan, moving west on both banks of the Wei.
translations.idiomatic: " He built pontoon bridges on the Wei, gave each man three days' rations, crossed with light horse, and sent the baggage west from Weinan along both banks.

sentences.zh: 十月壬辰，至沙苑。

translations.literal: On the day renchen of the tenth month they reached Shawei.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen of the tenth month they reached Shawei.

sentences.zh: 距齊軍六十餘里，神武引軍來會。

translations.literal: Sixty-odd li from the Qi army, the Divine Martial Emperor led his army to meet them.
translations.idiomatic: Sixty-odd li from the Qi army, the Divine Martial Emperor came to meet them.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，侯騎告齊軍至，帝召諸將謀。

translations.literal: On the day guisi, outriders reported the Qi army had arrived; the Emperor summoned the generals to consult.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi, scouts reported the Qi army had arrived, and the Emperor called the generals to council.

sentences.zh: 李弼曰：「彼眾我寡，不可平地置陣。

translations.literal: Li Bi said: "They are many and we are few; we cannot set battle lines on open ground.
translations.idiomatic: Li Bi said, "They outnumber us; we cannot fight on open ground.

sentences.zh: 此東十里，有渭曲，可先據以待之。

translations.literal: Ten li east of here is a bend of the Wei; we can seize it first and wait for them.
translations.idiomatic: Ten li east is a bend of the Wei; let us seize it and wait.

sentences.zh: 」遂進至渭，背水東西為陣。

translations.literal: " They then advanced to the Wei and formed lines east and west with the river at their backs.
translations.idiomatic: " They advanced to the Wei and formed lines east and west with the river at their backs.

sentences.zh: 李弼為右拒，趙貴為左拒。

translations.literal: Li Bi held the right refusal, Zhao Gui the left refusal.
translations.idiomatic: Li Bi held the right wing, Zhao Gui the left.

sentences.zh: 命將士皆偃戈於葭蘆中，聞鼓聲而起。

translations.literal: He ordered the officers and soldiers to lay their weapons in the rushes and rise at the sound of the drum.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the men to hide their weapons in the rushes and rise at the drum.

sentences.zh: 日晡，齊師至，望見軍少，競萃於左，軍亂不成列。

translations.literal: In the late afternoon the Qi army arrived; seeing few troops, they all crowded to the left, and the army fell into disorder without forming ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the day the Qi army came; seeing few troops, they crowded left and broke ranks.

sentences.zh: 兵將交，帝鳴鼓，士皆奮起。

translations.literal: As the armies were about to clash, the Emperor sounded the drum and the soldiers all leaped up.
translations.idiomatic: As battle was about to join, the Emperor beat the drum and the men leaped up.

sentences.zh: 於謹等六軍與之合戰，李弼等率鐵騎橫擊之。

translations.literal: Yu Jin's six armies joined them in battle, and Li Bi and the others led armored cavalry in a flanking strike.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Jin's six armies joined the fight, and Li Bi led armored cavalry in a flanking strike.

sentences.zh: 絕其軍為二，遂大破之，斬六千餘級，臨陣降者二萬餘人。

translations.literal: They cut the enemy army in two and routed it completely, beheading more than six thousand and taking more than twenty thousand who surrendered on the field.
translations.idiomatic: They cut the enemy in two and broke them utterly, beheading more than six thousand and taking more than twenty thousand on the field.

sentences.zh: 神武夜遁，追至河上，復大克。

translations.literal: The Divine Martial Emperor fled by night; they pursued to the river and won another great victory.
translations.idiomatic: The Divine Martial Emperor fled by night; they pursued to the river and won again.

sentences.zh: 前後虜其卒七萬，留其甲兵二萬，余悉縱歸。

translations.literal: In all they captured seventy thousand of his soldiers, kept twenty thousand in armor and arms, and released the rest.
translations.idiomatic: In all they took seventy thousand prisoners, kept twenty thousand in arms, and released the rest.

sentences.zh: 收其輜重兵甲，獻俘長安。

translations.literal: They gathered the baggage, armor, and weapons and presented the captives at Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: They gathered the baggage and arms and presented the captives at Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 李穆曰：「高歡膽破矣，逐之可獲。」

translations.literal: Li Mu said: "Gao Huan's courage is broken; pursue him and he can be taken."
translations.idiomatic: Li Mu said, "Gao Huan's courage is broken; pursue and we can take him."

sentences.zh: 帝不聽，乃還軍渭南。

translations.literal: The Emperor would not listen and returned the army to Weinan.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor would not listen and brought the army back to Weinan.

sentences.zh: 時所征諸州兵始至。

translations.literal: At that time the troops called up from the provinces were just arriving.
translations.idiomatic: The provincial troops called up were only just arriving.

sentences.zh: 乃於戰所，準當時兵，人種樹一株，栽柳七千根，以旌武功。

translations.literal: At the battlefield he had each soldier of the day plant one tree; seven thousand willows were planted to mark the military achievement.
translations.idiomatic: On the battlefield he had each soldier plant a tree; seven thousand willows marked the victory.

sentences.zh: 魏帝進帝柱國大將軍，增邑並前五千戶。

translations.literal: The Wei Emperor promoted the Emperor to Pillar of State and Grand General and increased his fief by five thousand households, making five thousand in all with what he already held.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei Emperor made the Emperor Pillar of State and Grand General and added five thousand households to his fief.

sentences.zh: 李弼等十二將，亦進爵增邑。

translations.literal: Li Bi and the other twelve generals also had their ranks and fiefs increased.
translations.idiomatic: Li Bi and the other twelve generals also received higher rank and larger fiefs.

sentences.zh: 以左僕射、馮翊王元季海為行臺，與開府獨孤信帥步騎二萬向洛陽。

translations.literal: Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, Prince of Fengyi Yuan Jihai, was made Commissioner and, with Director Dugu Xin, led twenty thousand foot and horse toward Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Left Vice Director Prince of Fengyi Yuan Jihai was made Commissioner and, with Director Dugu Xin, led twenty thousand foot and horse toward Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 賀拔勝、李弼度河圍蒲阪。

translations.literal: Heluo Sheng and Li Bi crossed the river and besieged Puyang.
translations.idiomatic: Heluo Sheng and Li Bi crossed the river and besieged Puyang.

sentences.zh: 蒲阪鎮將高子信開門納勝軍，東魏將薛崇禮棄城走，勝等追獲之。

translations.literal: The garrison commander of Puyang, Gao Zixin, opened the gates to Sheng's army; the Eastern Wei general Xue Chongli abandoned the city and fled, and Sheng and the others pursued and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: Garrison commander Gao Zixin opened the gates to Sheng; Eastern Wei general Xue Chongli fled, and Sheng pursued and captured him.

sentences.zh: 帝進軍蒲阪，略定汾、絳。

translations.literal: The Emperor advanced to Puyang and pacified Fen and Jiang.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor advanced to Puyang and pacified Fen and Jiang.

sentences.zh: 初，帝自弘農入關後，東魏將高昂圍弘農。

translations.literal: Earlier, after the Emperor entered the pass from Hongnong, the Eastern Wei general Gao Ao besieged Hongnong.
translations.idiomatic: After the Emperor entered the pass from Hongnong, Eastern Wei general Gao Ao besieged Hongnong.

sentences.zh: 聞其軍敗，退守洛陽。

translations.literal: When he heard their army had been defeated, he withdrew to hold Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of the defeat, he withdrew to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 獨孤信至新安，昂復走度河，遂入洛陽。

translations.literal: When Dugu Xin reached Xin'an, Ao fled again across the river, and Xin then entered Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Dugu Xin reached Xin'an, Ao fled across the river again, and Xin entered Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 自梁、陳已西，將吏降者相屬。

translations.literal: From Liang and Chen westward, commanders and officials surrendered one after another.
translations.idiomatic: From Liang and Chen westward, officials and commanders surrendered in succession.

sentences.zh: 於是東魏將堯雄、趙育、是雲寶出潁川，欲復降地。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Eastern Wei generals Yao Xiong, Zhao Yu, and Shiyun Bao came out of Yingchuan, intending to recover the surrendered territory.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Wei generals Yao Xiong, Zhao Yu, and Shiyun Bao came out of Yingchuan to recover lost ground.

sentences.zh: 帝遣儀同宇文貴、梁遷等逆擊，大破之，趙育來降。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent Commissioners Yuwen Gui, Liang Qian, and others to meet and attack them, routing them completely; Zhao Yu came over in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent Commissioners Yuwen Gui and Liang Qian against them, broke them utterly, and Zhao Yu surrendered.

sentences.zh: 東魏復遣任祥率河南兵與堯雄合，儀同怡峰與貴、遷等復擊破之。

translations.literal: Eastern Wei again sent Ren Xiang with Henan troops to join Yao Xiong; Commissioner Yi Feng with Gui and Qian again defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Wei sent Ren Xiang with Henan troops to join Yao Xiong; Commissioner Yi Feng with Gui and Qian defeated them again.

sentences.zh: 又遣都督韋孝寬取豫州。

translations.literal: He also sent Commander Wei Xiaokuan to take Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent Commander Wei Xiaokuan to take Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 是雲寶殺其東揚州刺史那椿，以州來降。

translations.literal: Shiyun Bao killed the Eastern Wei Governor of Eastern Yangzhou, Na Chun, and surrendered the province.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyun Bao killed Eastern Wei Governor of Eastern Yangzhou Na Chun and surrendered the province.

sentences.zh: 四年三月，帝率諸將入朝，禮畢還華州。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fourth year the Emperor led the generals to court; when the rites were complete he returned to Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of year four the Emperor led the generals to court and returned to Huazhou when the rites were done.

sentences.zh: 七月，東魏將侯景等圍獨孤信於洛陽，齊神武繼之。

translations.literal: In the seventh month the Eastern Wei general Hou Jing and others besieged Dugu Xin at Luoyang, and the Divine Martial Emperor of Qi followed after.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Eastern Wei general Hou Jing besieged Dugu Xin at Luoyang, and the Divine Martial Emperor of Qi followed.

sentences.zh: 帝奉魏帝至谷城，臨陣斬東魏將莫多婁貸文，悉虜其眾，送弘農。

translations.literal: The Emperor escorted the Wei Emperor to Gucheng, beheaded the Eastern Wei general Modu Lou Daiwen on the field, captured his whole force, and sent them to Hongnong.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor escorted the Wei Emperor to Gucheng, beheaded Eastern Wei general Modu Lou Daiwen on the field, took his whole force, and sent them to Hongnong.

sentences.zh: 遂進軍瀍東。

translations.literal: He then advanced to the east bank of the Chan.
translations.idiomatic: He then advanced to the east bank of the Chan.

sentences.zh: 景等夜解圍去。

translations.literal: Jing and the others broke the siege by night and left.
translations.idiomatic: Jing and the others broke the siege by night and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 及旦，帝率輕騎追至河上。

translations.literal: At dawn the Emperor led light cavalry in pursuit to the river.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the Emperor led light horse in pursuit to the river.

sentences.zh: 景等北據河橋，南屬芒山為陣，與諸軍戰。

translations.literal: Jing and the others held the north at Heqiao and linked their lines south to Mangshan, forming battle lines and fighting the armies.
translations.idiomatic: Jing and the others held Heqiao in the north and linked south to Mangshan, forming lines and giving battle.

sentences.zh: 帝馬中流矢，驚逸，軍中擾亂。

translations.literal: The Emperor's horse was struck by a flying arrow, bolted in panic, and the army fell into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor's horse took a stray arrow, bolted, and the army fell into disorder.

sentences.zh: 都督李穆下馬授帝，軍復振。

translations.literal: Commander Li Mu dismounted and gave the Emperor his horse; the army rallied.
translations.idiomatic: Commander Li Mu dismounted and gave the Emperor his horse, and the army rallied.

sentences.zh: 於是大捷，斬其將高昂、李猛、宋顯等，虜其甲士一萬五千人，赴河死者萬數。

translations.literal: Thereupon came a great victory; they beheaded the generals Gao Ao, Li Meng, Song Xian, and others, captured fifteen thousand armored soldiers, and ten thousand drowned fleeing into the river.
translations.idiomatic: They won a great victory, beheading Gao Ao, Li Meng, Song Xian, and others, taking fifteen thousand armored men, while ten thousand drowned fleeing into the river.

sentences.zh: 是日，置陣既大，首尾懸遠，從旦至未，戰數十合，氛霧四塞，莫能相知。

translations.literal: That day the battle lines were so vast that front and rear were far apart; from morning until dusk they fought several dozen engagements, and mist and fog filled the field so that none could tell friend from foe.
translations.idiomatic: That day the lines were vast and front and rear far apart; from morning to dusk they fought dozens of rounds in fog so thick none could tell friend from foe.

sentences.zh: 獨孤信、李遠居右，趙貴、怡峰居左，戰並不利。

translations.literal: Dugu Xin and Li Yuan held the right, Zhao Gui and Yi Feng the left; both wings fought poorly.
translations.idiomatic: Dugu Xin and Li Yuan held the right, Zhao Gui and Yi Feng the left; both wings fared badly.

sentences.zh: 又未知魏帝及帝所在，皆棄其卒先歸。

translations.literal: Not knowing where the Wei Emperor and the Emperor were, all abandoned their troops and fled first.
translations.idiomatic: Not knowing where the Wei Emperor and the Emperor were, all abandoned their men and fled.

sentences.zh: 開府李虎、念賢等為後軍；

translations.literal: Directors Li Hu and Nian Xian commanded the rear guard;
translations.idiomatic: Directors Li Hu and Nian Xian held the rear;

sentences.zh: 遇信等退，即與俱還。

translations.literal: meeting Xin and the others in retreat, they turned back together.
translations.idiomatic: meeting Xin in retreat, they turned back with him.

sentences.zh: 由是班師，洛陽亦失守。

translations.literal: Thereupon the army withdrew, and Luoyang was lost as well.
translations.idiomatic: The army withdrew, and Luoyang was lost as well.

sentences.zh: 大軍至弘農，守將皆已棄城西走。

translations.literal: When the main army reached Hongnong, the defending commanders had already abandoned the city and fled west.
translations.idiomatic: When the main army reached Hongnong, the defenders had already abandoned the city and fled west.

sentences.zh: 所虜降卒在弘農者，因相與閉門拒守。

translations.literal: The surrendered soldiers held at Hongnong therefore joined together, closed the gates, and resisted.
translations.idiomatic: The surrendered soldiers at Hongnong closed the gates and resisted together.

sentences.zh: 進攻拔之，誅其魁首數百人。

translations.literal: An assault took the city, and several hundred ringleaders were executed.
translations.idiomatic: They stormed the city and executed several hundred ringleaders.

sentences.zh: 大軍之東伐也，關中留守兵少，而前後所虜東魏士卒，皆散在百姓間，乃謀亂。

translations.literal: When the main army marched east, few troops remained to guard Guanzhong, and the Eastern Wei soldiers captured earlier were scattered among the common people; they therefore plotted rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: When the main army marched east, Guanzhong was lightly garrisoned, and captured Eastern Wei soldiers scattered among the people plotted rebellion.

sentences.zh: 及李虎等至長安，計無所出。

translations.literal: When Li Hu and the others reached Chang'an, they could think of no plan.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Hu and the others reached Chang'an, they could think of no plan.

sentences.zh: 乃與太尉王盟、僕射周惠達輔魏太子出次渭北。

translations.literal: They therefore joined Grand Commandant Wang Meng and Vice Director Zhou Huida in escorting the Wei crown prince to halt north of the Wei.
translations.idiomatic: They joined Grand Commandant Wang Meng and Vice Director Zhou Huida in escorting the Wei crown prince to halt north of the Wei.

sentences.zh: 關中大震恐，百姓相剽劫。

translations.literal: Great terror seized Guanzhong, and the people turned to plundering one another.
translations.idiomatic: Terror seized Guanzhong, and the people turned to plundering one another.

sentences.zh: 於是沙苑所俘軍人趙青雀、雍州人於伏德等遂反。

translations.literal: Thereupon Zhao Qingque, a soldier captured at Shawei, and Yu Fude of Yongzhou and others rose in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Then Zhao Qingque, a soldier captured at Shawei, and Yu Fude of Yongzhou rose in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 青雀據長安子城，伏德保咸陽；

translations.literal: Qingque held the inner city of Chang'an, and Fude held Xianyang;
translations.idiomatic: Qingque held the inner city of Chang'an, and Fude held Xianyang;

sentences.zh: 與太守慕容思度各收降卒，以拒還師。

translations.literal: together with the Administrator Murong Sidu they gathered surrendered soldiers to block the returning army.
translations.idiomatic: with Administrator Murong Sidu they gathered surrendered soldiers to block the returning army.

sentences.zh: 長安城人皆相率拒青雀，每日接戰。

translations.literal: The people of Chang'an all banded together to resist Qingque and fought him daily.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Chang'an banded together against Qingque and fought him daily.

sentences.zh: 魏帝留止閿鄉，令帝討之。

translations.literal: The Wei Emperor halted at Wenxiang and ordered the Emperor to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei Emperor halted at Wenxiang and ordered the Emperor to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 長安父老見帝，且悲且喜曰：「不意今日，復得見公。

translations.literal: The elders of Chang'an, seeing the Emperor, wept and rejoiced together, saying: "We never thought that today we would see you again.
translations.idiomatic: The elders of Chang'an wept and rejoiced, saying, "We never thought we would see you again today.

sentences.zh: 」士女咸相賀。

translations.literal: " Men and women alike congratulated one another.
translations.idiomatic: " Men and women alike congratulated one another.

sentences.zh: 華州刺史宇文導襲咸陽，斬思度，禽伏德，南度渭，與帝會，攻破青雀。

translations.literal: Governor of Huazhou Yuwen Dao raided Xianyang, beheaded Sidu, captured Fude, crossed the Wei southward, joined the Emperor, and broke Qingque.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Yuwen Dao raided Xianyang, beheaded Sidu, captured Fude, crossed south of the Wei, joined the Emperor, and broke Qingque.

sentences.zh: 太傅梁景睿先以疾留長安，遂與青雀通謀。

translations.literal: Grand Tutor Liang Jingrui had earlier remained at Chang'an because of illness and therefore conspired with Qingque.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor Liang Jingrui, left at Chang'an through illness, had conspired with Qingque.

sentences.zh: 至是亦伏誅，關中乃定。

translations.literal: At this time he too was executed, and Guanzhong was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: He too was executed, and Guanzhong was pacified.

sentences.zh: 魏帝還長安，帝復屯華州。

translations.literal: The Wei Emperor returned to Chang'an, and the Emperor again encamped at Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei Emperor returned to Chang'an, and the Emperor encamped again at Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 十二月，是雲寶襲洛陽，東魏將王元軌棄城走。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Shiyun Bao raided Luoyang; the Eastern Wei general Wang Yuangui abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Shiyun Bao raided Luoyang; Eastern Wei general Wang Yuangui abandoned the city and fled.

sentences.zh: 都督趙剛襲廣州拔之。

translations.literal: Commander Zhao Gang raided Guangzhou and took it.
translations.idiomatic: Commander Zhao Gang raided Guangzhou and took it.

sentences.zh: 自襄、廣以西城鎮復西屬。

translations.literal: From Xiang and Guang westward, the fortified towns again submitted to the west.
translations.idiomatic: From Xiang and Guang westward, the fortified towns again submitted to the west.

sentences.zh: 五年冬，大閱於華陰。

translations.literal: In the winter of the fifth year a grand review was held at Huayin.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of year five a grand review was held at Huayin.

sentences.zh: 六年春，東魏將侯景出三鴉，將侵荊州。

translations.literal: In the spring of the sixth year the Eastern Wei general Hou Jing came out of Sanya, intending to invade Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of year six Eastern Wei general Hou Jing came out of Sanya to invade Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 帝遣開府李弼、獨孤信各率騎出武關，景乃還。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent Directors Li Bi and Dugu Xin, each leading cavalry out through Wuguan; Jing then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent Directors Li Bi and Dugu Xin with cavalry out through Wuguan, and Jing withdrew.

sentences.zh: 夏，蠕蠕度河至夏州，帝召諸軍屯沙苑以備之。

translations.literal: In summer the Rouran crossed the river to Xiazhou; the Emperor summoned the armies to encamp at Shawei in defense.
translations.idiomatic: In summer the Rouran crossed the river to Xiazhou; the Emperor summoned the armies to Shawei in defense.

sentences.zh: 七年十一月，帝奏行十二條制，恐百官不勉於職事，又下令申明之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the seventh year the Emperor memorialized twelve regulations for enactment, fearing that officials would not exert themselves in their duties, and also issued orders to clarify them.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of year seven the Emperor memorialized twelve regulations, fearing officials would slack in duty, and issued clarifying orders.

sentences.zh: 八年十月，齊神武侵汾、絳，圍玉壁。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the eighth year the Divine Martial Emperor of Qi invaded Fen and Jiang and besieged Yubi.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of year eight the Divine Martial Emperor of Qi invaded Fen and Jiang and besieged Yubi.

sentences.zh: 帝出軍蒲阪，神武退；

translations.literal: The Emperor led his army out at Puyang; the Divine Martial Emperor withdrew;
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor led his army out at Puyang; the Divine Martial Emperor withdrew;

sentences.zh: 度汾追之，遂遁去。

translations.literal: crossing the Fen in pursuit, he then fled away.
translations.idiomatic: crossing the Fen in pursuit, the Emperor drove him off.

sentences.zh: 十二月，魏帝狩於華陰，大饗將士。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month the Wei Emperor hunted at Huayin and held a great feast for the officers and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month the Wei Emperor hunted at Huayin and feasted the officers and soldiers.

sentences.zh: 帝帥諸將，朝於行在所。

translations.literal: The Emperor led the generals to attend upon him at his temporary residence.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor led the generals to attend him at his temporary residence.

sentences.zh: 九年二月，東魏北豫州刺史高慎舉州來附，帝帥師迎之。

translations.literal: In the second month of the ninth year the Eastern Wei Governor of Beiyu, Gao Shen, surrendered the province; the Emperor led his army to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of year nine Eastern Wei Governor of Beiyu Gao Shen surrendered the province, and the Emperor led his army to welcome him.

sentences.zh: 三月，齊神武據芒山陣，不進者數日。

translations.literal: In the third month the Divine Martial Emperor of Qi took position on Mangshan and did not advance for several days.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month the Divine Martial Emperor of Qi held Mangshan and did not advance for days.

sentences.zh: 帝留輜重於瀍曲，軍士銜枚，夜登芒山，未明擊之。

translations.literal: The Emperor left the baggage at the bend of the Chan; the soldiers took sticks in their mouths, climbed Mangshan by night, and attacked before dawn.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor left the baggage at the bend of the Chan; the men climbed Mangshan by night with sticks in their mouths and struck before dawn.

sentences.zh: 神武單騎為賀拔勝所逐，僅免。

translations.literal: The Divine Martial Emperor, alone on horseback, was pursued by Heluo Sheng and barely escaped.
translations.idiomatic: The Divine Martial Emperor, alone on horseback, was pursued by Heluo Sheng and barely escaped.

sentences.zh: 帝率右軍若干惠，大破神武軍，悉虜其步卒。

translations.literal: The Emperor led the right wing under Ruogan Hui and routed the Divine Martial Emperor's army completely, capturing all his foot soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor led the right wing under Ruogan Hui and routed the Divine Martial Emperor's army, taking all his foot soldiers.

sentences.zh: 趙貴等五將軍居左，戰不利。

translations.literal: Zhao Gui and five other generals held the left; the fighting went badly.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Gui and five other generals held the left, and the fighting went badly.

sentences.zh: 神武復合戰，帝又不利，夜引還。

translations.literal: The Divine Martial Emperor rallied and fought again; the Emperor was again at a disadvantage and withdrew by night.
translations.idiomatic: The Divine Martial Emperor rallied and fought again; the Emperor was again at a disadvantage and withdrew by night.

sentences.zh: 入關，屯渭上。

translations.literal: Entering the pass, he encamped on the Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Entering the pass, he encamped on the Wei.

sentences.zh: 神武進至陜，開府達奚武等禦之，乃退。

translations.literal: The Divine Martial Emperor advanced to Shaan; Directors Daxi Wu and others held him off, and he withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The Divine Martial Emperor advanced to Shaan; Directors Daxi Wu and others held him off, and he withdrew.

sentences.zh: 帝以芒山諸將失律，上表自貶，魏帝不許。

translations.literal: Because the Mangshan generals had violated discipline, the Emperor memorialized asking to demote himself; the Wei Emperor would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Because the Mangshan generals had violated discipline, the Emperor memorialized asking to demote himself; the Wei Emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 於是廣募關、隴豪右，以增軍旅。

translations.literal: Thereupon he broadly recruited the leading families of Guan and Long to increase the army.
translations.idiomatic: He broadly recruited the leading families of Guan and Long to swell the army.

sentences.zh: 十月，大閱於櫟陽，還屯華州。

translations.literal: In the tenth month a grand review was held at Lueyang, and he returned to encamp at Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he held a grand review at Lueyang and returned to Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 十年五月，帝朝京師。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the tenth year the Emperor attended court at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of year ten the Emperor attended court at the capital.

sentences.zh: 七月，魏帝以帝前後所上二十四條及十二條新制，方為中興永式；

translations.literal: In the seventh month the Wei Emperor, because the twenty-four articles and twelve new regulations the Emperor had earlier submitted were to serve as the enduring model for restoration,
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month the Wei Emperor, taking the twenty-four articles and twelve new regulations the Emperor had submitted as the enduring model for restoration,

sentences.zh: 命尚書蘇綽更損益之，總為五卷，班於天下。

translations.literal: ordered Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat Su Chuo to revise them further; in all five scrolls were compiled and promulgated throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: ordered Vice Director Su Chuo to revise them further; five scrolls were compiled and promulgated throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 於是搜簡賢才為牧、守、令，習新制而遣焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon worthy men were sought out and appointed governors, prefects, and magistrates; they were instructed in the new regulations and then sent out.
translations.idiomatic: Worthy men were sought out as governors, prefects, and magistrates, instructed in the new regulations, and sent out.

sentences.zh: 數年間，百姓便之。

translations.literal: Within a few years the common people found the system convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few years the people found the system convenient.

sentences.zh: 十月，大閱於白水。

translations.literal: In the tenth month a grand review was held at Baishui.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he held a grand review at Baishui.

sentences.zh: 十一年十月，大閱於白水，遂西狩岐陽。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the eleventh year a grand review was held at Baishui, and he then hunted west at Qiyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of year eleven he reviewed at Baishui and then hunted west at Qiyang.

sentences.zh: 十二年春，涼州刺史宇文仲和據州反，瓜州人張保害刺史成慶以應之，帝遣開府獨孤信討之。

translations.literal: In the spring of the twelfth year, Governor of Liangzhou Yuwen Zhonghe held the province in rebellion; Zhang Bao of Guazhou killed the Governor Cheng Qing in response; the Emperor sent Director Dugu Xin to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of year twelve, Governor Yuwen Zhonghe rebelled at Liangzhou, and Zhang Bao of Guazhou killed Governor Cheng Qing in response; the Emperor sent Director Dugu Xin against them.

sentences.zh: 東魏將侯景侵襄州，帝遣開府若干惠禦之，至穰，景遁去。

translations.literal: The Eastern Wei general Hou Jing invaded Xiangzhou; the Emperor sent Director Ruogan Hui to hold him off; when Hui reached Xiang, Jing withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Wei general Hou Jing invaded Xiangzhou; the Emperor sent Director Ruogan Hui against him; at Xiang, Jing withdrew.

sentences.zh: 五月，獨孤信平涼州，禽仲和，遷其百姓六千餘家於長安。

translations.literal: In the fifth month Dugu Xin pacified Liangzhou, captured Zhonghe, and moved more than six thousand of his households to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Dugu Xin pacified Liangzhou, captured Zhonghe, and moved more than six thousand households to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 瓜州都督令狐延起義誅張保，瓜州平。

translations.literal: Commander of Guazhou Linghu Yanqi raised a righteous force, executed Zhang Bao, and Guazhou was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Commander Linghu Yanqi of Guazhou rose in righteous force, executed Zhang Bao, and Guazhou was pacified.

sentences.zh: 七月，帝大會諸軍於咸陽。

translations.literal: In the seventh month the Emperor held a great assembly of the armies at Xianyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month the Emperor held a great assembly of the armies at Xianyang.

sentences.zh: 十三年正月，東魏河南大行臺侯景舉河南六州來附，被圍於潁川。

translations.literal: In the first month of the thirteenth year, Hou Jing, Grand Commissioner of Henan of Eastern Wei, surrendered the six Henan provinces and came over, but was besieged at Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of year thirteen, Hou Jing, Grand Commissioner of Henan of Eastern Wei, surrendered the six Henan provinces but was besieged at Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 六月，帝遣開府李弼援之，東魏將韓軌等遁去。

translations.literal: In the sixth month the Emperor sent Director Li Bi to relieve him; the Eastern Wei generals Han Gui and others withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month the Emperor sent Director Li Bi to relieve him; Eastern Wei generals Han Gui and others withdrew.

sentences.zh: 景遂徙鎮豫州。

translations.literal: Jing then moved his garrison to Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jing then moved his garrison to Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 於是遣開府王思政據潁川，弼引軍還。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Emperor sent Director Wang Sizheng to hold Yingchuan, and Bi led his army back.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent Director Wang Sizheng to hold Yingchuan, and Bi led his army back.

sentences.zh: 七月，侯景密圖附梁，帝知其謀，悉追還前後所配景將士。

translations.literal: In the seventh month Hou Jing secretly plotted to submit to Liang; the Emperor learned of the plan and recalled all the officers and soldiers previously assigned to Jing.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Hou Jing secretly plotted to submit to Liang; the Emperor learned of it and recalled all officers and soldiers previously assigned to Jing.

sentences.zh: 景懼，遂叛。

translations.literal: Jing was afraid and rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Jing was afraid and rebelled.

sentences.zh: 冬，帝奉魏帝西狩咸陽。

translations.literal: In winter the Emperor escorted the Wei Emperor on a western hunt at Xianyang.
translations.idiomatic: In winter the Emperor escorted the Wei Emperor on a western hunt at Xianyang.

sentences.zh: 十四年春，魏帝詔封帝長子覺為寧都郡公。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fourteenth year the Wei Emperor issued an edict enfeoffing the Emperor's eldest son Jue as Duke of Ningdu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of year fourteen the Wei Emperor enfeoffed the Emperor's eldest son Jue as Duke of Ningdu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 初，帝以平元顥納孝莊帝功，封寧都縣子。

translations.literal: Earlier, for the merit of receiving Emperor Xiaozhuang when Yuan Hao was pacified, the Emperor had been enfeoffed as Viscount of Ningdu County.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, for receiving Emperor Xiaozhuang when Yuan Hao was pacified, the Emperor had been enfeoffed as Viscount of Ningdu County.

sentences.zh: 至是，改以為郡，以封覺，用彰勤王之始也。

translations.literal: At this time it was changed to a commandery and given to Jue, to mark the beginning of his service to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: It was now changed to a commandery and given to Jue, to mark the beginning of his service to the throne.

sentences.zh: 五月，魏帝進帝位太師。

translations.literal: In the fifth month the Wei Emperor promoted the Emperor to Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month the Wei Emperor promoted the Emperor to Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 帝奉魏太子巡撫西境，登隴，刻石紀事。

translations.literal: The Emperor escorted the Wei crown prince on a tour of the western frontier, ascended Long, and carved stone to record the event.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor escorted the Wei crown prince on a tour of the western frontier, ascended Long, and carved stone to record the event.

sentences.zh: 遂至原州，歷北長城，大狩。

translations.literal: He then went to Yuanzhou, followed the northern Long Wall, and held a great hunt.
translations.idiomatic: He then went to Yuanzhou, followed the northern Long Wall, and held a great hunt.

sentences.zh: 東趣五原，至蒲州，聞魏帝不豫而還。

translations.literal: Turning east toward Wuyuan, he reached Puzhou; hearing that the Wei Emperor was unwell, he returned.
translations.idiomatic: Turning east toward Wuyuan, he reached Puzhou; hearing the Wei Emperor was unwell, he returned.

sentences.zh: 及至，魏帝疾已愈，乃還華州。

translations.literal: When he arrived, the Wei Emperor's illness had already improved, and he returned to Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived, the Wei Emperor had already recovered, and he returned to Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 是歲，東魏將高嶽圍王思政於潁川。

translations.literal: That year the Eastern Wei general Gao Yue besieged Wang Sizheng at Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: That year Eastern Wei general Gao Yue besieged Wang Sizheng at Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 十五年春，帝遣大將軍趙貴帥師援王思政。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fifteenth year the Emperor sent Grand General Zhao Gui to lead troops to relieve Wang Sizheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of year fifteen the Emperor sent Grand General Zhao Gui to relieve Wang Sizheng.

sentences.zh: 高嶽堰洧水以灌城，潁川以北皆為陂澤，救兵不得至。

translations.literal: Gao Yue dammed the Wei River to flood the city; north of Yingchuan all became marsh and lake, and relief troops could not reach it.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yue dammed the Wei River to flood the city; north of Yingchuan all became marsh, and relief could not reach it.

sentences.zh: 六月，潁川陷。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Yingchuan fell.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Yingchuan fell.

sentences.zh: 初，侯景圍建鄴，梁司州刺史柳仲禮赴臺城。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Hou Jing besieged Jiankang, Liang Governor of Sizhou Liu Zhongli went to relieve the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Hou Jing besieged Jiankang, Liang Governor of Sizhou Liu Zhongli went to relieve the capital.

sentences.zh: 梁竟陵郡守孫皓以郡內附，帝使大都督苻貴鎮之。

translations.literal: Sun Hao, Administrator of Jingling Commandery of Liang, submitted the commandery; the Emperor sent Grand Commander Fu Gui to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hao, Administrator of Jingling of Liang, submitted the commandery; the Emperor sent Grand Commander Fu Gui to garrison it.

sentences.zh: 及建鄴陷，仲禮還司州，來寇。

translations.literal: When Jiankang fell, Zhongli returned to Sizhou and came to raid.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiankang fell, Zhongli returned to Sizhou and came to raid.

sentences.zh: 皓以郡叛，帝大怒。

translations.literal: Hao rebelled with the commandery; the Emperor was greatly angered.
translations.idiomatic: Hao rebelled with the commandery, and the Emperor was greatly angered.

sentences.zh: 十一月，遣開府楊忠攻克隨州，進圍仲禮長史馬岫於安陸。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month he sent Director Yang Zhong to take Suizhou and advanced to besiege Zhongli's chief clerk Ma Xiu at Anlu.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he sent Director Yang Zhong to take Suizhou and besieged Zhongli's chief clerk Ma Xiu at Anlu.

sentences.zh: 十六年正月，仲禮來援安陸，楊忠逆擊於漴頭，大破之，禽仲禮。

translations.literal: In the first month of the sixteenth year Zhongli came to relieve Anlu; Yang Zhong met and attacked him at Chongtou, routed him completely, and captured Zhongli.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of year sixteen Zhongli came to relieve Anlu; Yang Zhong met him at Chongtou, broke him utterly, and captured Zhongli.

sentences.zh: 馬岫以城降。

translations.literal: Ma Xiu surrendered the city.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Xiu surrendered the city.

sentences.zh: 三月，魏帝封帝第二子震為武邑公。

translations.literal: In the third month the Wei Emperor enfeoffed the Emperor's second son Zhen as Duke of Wuyi.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month the Wei Emperor enfeoffed the Emperor's second son Zhen as Duke of Wuyi.

sentences.zh: 七月，帝東伐，拜章武公導為大將軍，總督留守諸軍，屯涇北，鎮關中。

translations.literal: In the seventh month the Emperor marched east; he appointed Duke of Zhangwu Dao Grand General and put him in overall command of the garrison forces, encamped north of Jing, and held Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month the Emperor marched east; he made Duke of Zhangwu Dao Grand General, put him in command of the garrison, encamped north of Jing, and held Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 九月丁巳，軍出長安。

translations.literal: On the day dingsi of the ninth month the army set out from Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi of the ninth month the army set out from Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 連雨，自秋及冬，諸軍馬驢多死。

translations.literal: Rain fell continuously from autumn through winter, and many army horses and donkeys died.
translations.idiomatic: Rain fell continuously from autumn through winter, and many horses and donkeys died.

sentences.zh: 遂於弘農北造橋濟河，自蒲阪還。

translations.literal: He then built a bridge north of Hongnong to cross the river and returned from Puyang.
translations.idiomatic: He built a bridge north of Hongnong to cross the river and returned from Puyang.

sentences.zh: 於是河南自洛陽，河北自平陽以東，遂入齊。

translations.literal: Thereupon from Luoyang in Henan and from Pingyang east in Hebei, the territory passed into Qi.
translations.idiomatic: From Luoyang in Henan and from Pingyang east in Hebei, the territory passed into Qi.

sentences.zh: 十七年三月，魏文帝崩，皇太子嗣位，帝以冢宰總百揆。

translations.literal: In the third month of the seventeenth year Emperor Wen of Wei died; the crown prince succeeded, and the Emperor as Grand Minister directed all affairs of state.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of year seventeen Emperor Wen of Wei died; the crown prince succeeded, and the Emperor as Grand Minister directed all affairs.

sentences.zh: 十月，帝遣大將軍王雄出子午，伐上津、魏興，大將軍達奚武出散關，伐南鄭。

translations.literal: In the tenth month the Emperor sent Grand General Wang Xiong out through Ziwu to attack Shangjin and Weixing, and Grand General Daxi Wu out through San'guan to attack Nanzheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he sent Grand General Wang Xiong out through Ziwu against Shangjin and Weixing, and Grand General Daxi Wu out through San'guan against Nanzheng.

sentences.zh: 廢帝元年春，王雄平上津、魏興，以其地置東梁州。

translations.literal: In the spring of the first year of the Deposed Emperor, Wang Xiong pacified Shangjin and Weixing and established Eastern Liangzhou on that territory.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of Deposed Emperor year one, Wang Xiong pacified Shangjin and Weixing and established Eastern Liangzhou there.

sentences.zh: 四月，達奚武圍南鄭。

translations.literal: In the fourth month Daxi Wu besieged Nanzheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Daxi Wu besieged Nanzheng.

sentences.zh: 月餘，梁州刺史宜豐侯蕭修以州降武。

translations.literal: After more than a month, Liang Governor Marquis of Yifeng Xiao Xiu surrendered the province to Wu.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a month, Liang Governor Marquis of Yifeng Xiao Xiu surrendered the province to Wu.

sentences.zh: 八月，東梁州百姓圍州城，帝復遣王雄討之。

translations.literal: In the eighth month the people of Eastern Liangzhou besieged the provincial city; the Emperor again sent Wang Xiong to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month the people of Eastern Liangzhou besieged the provincial city, and the Emperor again sent Wang Xiong against them.

sentences.zh: 二年正月，魏帝詔帝為左丞相、大行臺、都督中外諸軍事。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year the Wei Emperor issued an edict appointing the Emperor Left Chancellor, Grand Commissioner, and Director of All Armies at Home and Abroad.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of year two the Wei Emperor appointed the Emperor Left Chancellor, Grand Commissioner, and Director of All Armies at Home and Abroad.

sentences.zh: 二月，東梁州平，遷其豪帥於雍州。

translations.literal: In the second month Eastern Liangzhou was pacified, and its chieftains were moved to Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Eastern Liangzhou was pacified, and its chieftains were moved to Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 三月，帝遣大將軍、魏安公尉遲迥帥師伐梁武陵王蕭紀於蜀。

translations.literal: In the third month the Emperor sent Grand General Duke of Wei'an Wei Chiji to lead troops against Liang Prince of Wuling Xiao Ji in Shu.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month he sent Grand General Duke of Wei'an Wei Chiji against Liang Prince of Wuling Xiao Ji in Shu.

sentences.zh: 四月，帝勒銳騎三萬，西逾隴，度金城河，至姑臧。

translations.literal: In the fourth month the Emperor led thirty thousand sharp horsemen west over Long, crossed the Jincheng River, and reached Guzang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month the Emperor led thirty thousand sharp horse west over Long, crossed the Jincheng River, and reached Guzang.

sentences.zh: 吐谷渾震懼，遣使獻其方物。

translations.literal: Tuyuhun was terrified and sent envoys presenting local products.
translations.idiomatic: Tuyuhun was terrified and sent envoys with local tribute.

sentences.zh: 七月，帝至自姑臧。

translations.literal: In the seventh month the Emperor returned from Guzang.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month the Emperor returned from Guzang.

sentences.zh: 八月，尉遲迥克成都，劍南平。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Wei Chiji took Chengdu and pacified Jiannan.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Wei Chiji took Chengdu and pacified Jiannan.

sentences.zh: 十一月，尚書元烈謀亂，伏誅。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Vice Director Yuan Lie plotted rebellion and was executed.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Vice Director Yuan Lie plotted rebellion and was executed.

sentences.zh: 三年正月，始作九命之典，以敘內外官爵。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year the Nine Ranks system was first established to order inner and outer offices and ranks.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of year three the Nine Ranks system was first established to order inner and outer offices and ranks.

sentences.zh: 以第一品為九命，第九品為一命；

translations.literal: The first rank was made nine orders, and the ninth rank one order;
translations.idiomatic: The first rank was made nine orders, and the ninth rank one order;

sentences.zh: 改流外品為九秩，亦以九為上。

translations.literal: ranks outside the regular flow were also made nine grades, with nine again as the highest.
translations.idiomatic: ranks outside the regular flow were also made nine grades, with nine as the highest.

sentences.zh: 又改置州、郡、縣，凡改州四十六，置州一，改郡一百六，改縣三百三十。

translations.literal: Provinces, commanderies, and counties were also reorganized; in all forty-six provinces were renamed, one province established, one hundred six commanderies renamed, and three hundred thirty counties renamed.
translations.idiomatic: Provinces, commanderies, and counties were reorganized; forty-six provinces were renamed, one established, one hundred six commanderies renamed, and three hundred thirty counties renamed.

sentences.zh: 魏帝有怨言，於是帝與公卿議，廢帝；

translations.literal: The Wei Emperor voiced complaints; thereupon the Emperor consulted with the dukes and ministers and deposed the emperor;
translations.idiomatic: The Wei Emperor voiced complaints; the Emperor consulted with the dukes and ministers and deposed him;

sentences.zh: 立齊王廓。

translations.literal: Prince of Qi Kuo was raised instead.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Qi Kuo was raised instead.

sentences.zh: 是為恭帝。

translations.literal: This was Emperor Gong.
translations.idiomatic: This was Emperor Gong.

sentences.zh: 恭帝元年四月，帝大饗群臣。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the first year of Emperor Gong the Emperor held a great feast for the ministers.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Emperor Gong year one the Emperor held a great feast for the ministers.

sentences.zh: 魏史柳虬執簡書告於朝曰：「廢帝，文皇帝之嗣子，年七歲，文皇帝托於安定公曰：『是子也，才由於公；

translations.literal: The Wei historian Liu Qiu, holding the bamboo annals, announced in court: "The Deposed Emperor was the heir son of Emperor Wen; at seven years of age Emperor Wen entrusted him to the Duke of Anding, saying: 'This child's talent comes from you;
translations.idiomatic: Wei historian Liu Qiu, holding the bamboo annals, announced in court, "The Deposed Emperor was Emperor Wen's heir; at seven Emperor Wen entrusted him to the Duke of Anding, saying, 'This child's talent comes from you;

sentences.zh: 不才亦由於公，公宜勉之。

translations.literal: if he lacks talent, that too comes from you; you should exert yourself for him.
translations.idiomatic: if he lacks talent, that too comes from you; you should exert yourself for him.

sentences.zh: 』公既受茲重寄，居元輔之任，又納女為皇后；

translations.literal: " The Duke accepted this heavy trust and held the post of chief minister; he also gave his daughter in marriage as empress;
translations.idiomatic: " The Duke accepted this heavy trust and held the post of chief minister; he also gave his daughter in marriage as empress;

sentences.zh: 遂不能訓誨有成，致令廢黜，負文皇帝付屬之意，此咎非安定公而誰？

translations.literal: yet he could not instruct and guide him to achievement, causing his deposition, and failing the intent of Emperor Wen's entrustment; if not the Duke of Anding, who bears this blame?
translations.idiomatic: yet he could not instruct and guide him to achievement, causing his deposition, and failing Emperor Wen's entrustment; if not the Duke of Anding, who bears this blame?

sentences.zh: 」帝乃令太常盧辯作誥喻公卿曰：「嗚呼！

translations.literal: " The Emperor then ordered Grand Master of Ceremonies Lu Bian to compose an announcement to the dukes and ministers, saying: "Alas!
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor ordered Grand Master of Ceremonies Lu Bian to compose an announcement to the dukes and ministers, saying, "Alas!

sentences.zh: 我群後暨眾士，維文皇帝以繈褓之嗣托於予，訓之誨之，庶厥有成。

translations.literal: My lords and ministers, Emperor Wen entrusted his infant heir to me; I was to train and instruct him, hoping he would succeed.
translations.idiomatic: My lords and ministers, Emperor Wen entrusted his infant heir to me to train and instruct, hoping he would succeed.

sentences.zh: 而予罔能弗變厥心，庸暨乎廢墜我文皇帝之志。

translations.literal: Yet I could not change his heart, and so I have failed the intent of Emperor Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I could not change his heart, and so I have failed Emperor Wen's intent.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 茲咎予其焉避？

translations.literal: How can I escape this blame?
translations.idiomatic: How can I escape this blame?

sentences.zh: 予實知之，矧爾眾人之心哉。

translations.literal: I know it myself, and how much more do all your hearts know it.
translations.idiomatic: I know it myself, and all your hearts know it as well.

sentences.zh: 惟予之顏，豈惟今厚，將恐來世，以予為口實。

translations.literal: As for my face, it is not only shameful today; I fear future ages will take me as a byword.
translations.idiomatic: As for my face, it is shameful not only today; I fear future ages will take me as a byword.

sentences.zh: 」乙亥，魏帝詔封帝子邕為輔城公，憲為安城公。

translations.literal: On the day yihai the Wei Emperor issued an edict enfeoffing the Emperor's son Yong as Duke of Fucheng and Xian as Duke of Ancheng.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai the Wei Emperor enfeoffed the Emperor's son Yong as Duke of Fucheng and Xian as Duke of Ancheng.

sentences.zh: 七月，西狩至原州。

translations.literal: In the seventh month he hunted west as far as Yuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he hunted west as far as Yuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 梁元帝遣使請據舊圖以定疆界；

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan of Liang sent envoys asking to fix the borders according to the old maps;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan of Liang sent envoys asking to fix the borders according to the old maps;

sentences.zh: 又連結於齊，言辭悖慢。

translations.literal: he also allied with Qi, and his words were insolent and contemptuous.
translations.idiomatic: he also allied with Qi, and his words were insolent and contemptuous.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「古人有言，天之所棄，誰能興之，其蕭繹之謂乎。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "The ancients said that what Heaven abandons, who can restore? That must mean Xiao Yi.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "The ancients said that what Heaven abandons, who can restore? That must mean Xiao Yi.

sentences.zh: 」十月壬戌，遣柱國於謹、中山公護與大將軍楊忠、韋孝寬等步騎五萬討之。

translations.literal: " On the day renxu of the tenth month he sent Pillar of State Yu Jin, Duke of Zhongshan Hu, with Grand Generals Yang Zhong, Wei Xiaokuan, and others, twenty thousand foot and horse, to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: " On renxu of the tenth month he sent Pillar of State Yu Jin, Duke of Zhongshan Hu, with Grand Generals Yang Zhong, Wei Xiaokuan, and others, twenty thousand foot and horse, against him.

sentences.zh: 十一月癸未，師濟漢，中山公護與楊忠率銳騎先屯其城下。

translations.literal: On the day guiwei of the eleventh month the army crossed the Han; Duke of Zhongshan Hu with Yang Zhong led sharp cavalry to encamp first beneath the city walls.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei of the eleventh month the army crossed the Han; Duke of Zhongshan Hu with Yang Zhong led sharp horse to encamp first beneath the walls.

sentences.zh: 丙申，於謹至江陵，列營圍守。

translations.literal: On the day bingshen Yu Jin reached Jiangling and set camp in siege.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen Yu Jin reached Jiangling and set camp in siege.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，克其城，戕梁元帝，虜其百官士庶以歸，沒為奴婢者十餘萬，免者二百餘家。

translations.literal: On the day xinhai the city was taken; Emperor Yuan of Liang was killed; his hundred officials, gentry, and common people were captured and taken back; more than a hundred thousand were made slaves, and more than two hundred households were spared.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai the city was taken; Emperor Yuan of Liang was killed; his officials, gentry, and people were captured; more than a hundred thousand were made slaves, and more than two hundred households were spared.

sentences.zh: 立蕭察為梁主，居江陵，為魏附庸。

translations.literal: Xiao Cha was established as ruler of Liang and dwelt at Jiangling as a vassal of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Cha was established as ruler of Liang at Jiangling as a vassal of Wei.

sentences.zh: 魏氏之初，統國三十六，大姓九十九，後多絕滅。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wei, thirty-six states were registered and ninety-nine great clans; later many died out.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Wei, thirty-six states and ninety-nine great clans were registered; later many died out.

sentences.zh: 至是，以諸將功高者為三十六國後；

translations.literal: At this time the generals of highest merit were made successors to the thirty-six states;
translations.idiomatic: Generals of highest merit were now made successors to the thirty-six states;

sentences.zh: 次者為九十九姓後；

translations.literal: those of next rank were made successors to the ninety-nine clans;
translations.idiomatic: those of next rank were made successors to the ninety-nine clans;

sentences.zh: 所統軍人，亦改從其姓。

translations.literal: the soldiers under their command also changed to bear their surnames.
translations.idiomatic: the soldiers under their command also took their surnames.

sentences.zh: 二年，梁廣州刺史王琳寇邊。

translations.literal: In the second year Wang Lin, Governor of Guangzhou of Liang, raided the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: In year two Wang Lin, Governor of Guangzhou of Liang, raided the frontier.

sentences.zh: 十月，帝遣大將軍豆盧寧帥師討之。

translations.literal: In the tenth month the Emperor sent Grand General Dou Lu'ning to lead troops against him.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the Emperor sent Grand General Dou Lu'ning against him.

sentences.zh: 三年正月丁丑，初行《周禮》，建六官，魏帝進帝位太師、大冢宰。

translations.literal: On the day dingchou of the first month of the third year the Rites of Zhou were first enacted, the Six Offices were established, and the Wei Emperor promoted the Emperor to Grand Preceptor and Grand Minister.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou of the first month of year three the Rites of Zhou were first enacted, the Six Offices established, and the Wei Emperor promoted the Emperor to Grand Preceptor and Grand Minister.

sentences.zh: 帝以漢、魏官繁，思革前弊。

translations.literal: The Emperor, seeing that Han and Wei offices were overly numerous, wished to reform earlier abuses.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that Han and Wei offices were overly numerous, the Emperor wished to reform earlier abuses.

sentences.zh: 大統中，乃令蘇綽、盧辯依周制改創其事，尋亦置六卿官，然為撰次未成，眾務猶歸臺閣。

translations.literal: During Datong he had ordered Su Chuo and Lu Bian to recreate the system according to the Zhou model; the Six Ministers were also soon established, but because the compilation was not yet complete, most affairs still returned to the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: During Datong he had ordered Su Chuo and Lu Bian to recreate the system on the Zhou model; the Six Ministers were also established, but with the compilation incomplete, most affairs still returned to the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 至是始畢，乃命行之。

translations.literal: Now it was finished, and he ordered it enacted.
translations.idiomatic: Now it was finished, and he ordered it enacted.

sentences.zh: 四月，帝北巡。

translations.literal: In the fourth month the Emperor toured north.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month the Emperor toured north.

sentences.zh: 七月，度北河。

translations.literal: In the seventh month he crossed the northern river.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he crossed the northern river.

sentences.zh: 魏帝封帝子直為秦郡公，招為正平公。

translations.literal: The Wei Emperor enfeoffed the Emperor's son Zhi as Duke of Qin Commandery and Zhao as Duke of Zhengping.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei Emperor enfeoffed the Emperor's son Zhi as Duke of Qin Commandery and Zhao as Duke of Zhengping.

sentences.zh: 九月，帝不豫，還至雲陽，命中山公護受遺輔嗣子。

translations.literal: In the ninth month the Emperor fell ill, returned to Yunyang, and ordered Duke of Zhongshan Hu to receive his final instructions and assist the heir.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the Emperor fell ill, returned to Yunyang, and ordered Duke of Zhongshan Hu to receive his final instructions and assist the heir.

sentences.zh: 十月乙亥，帝薨於雲陽宮，還長安發喪，時年五十。

translations.literal: On the day yihai of the tenth month the Emperor died at Yunyang Palace; the body was brought back to Chang'an and mourning was proclaimed; he was fifty years old.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai of the tenth month the Emperor died at Yunyang Palace; the body was brought to Chang'an and mourning proclaimed; he was fifty.

sentences.zh: 十二月甲申，葬於成陵，謚文公。

translations.literal: On the day jiashen of the twelfth month he was buried at Chengling; his posthumous title was Duke Wen.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen of the twelfth month he was buried at Chengling with the posthumous title Duke Wen.

sentences.zh: 及孝閔帝受禪，追尊為文王，廟曰太祖。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin received the throne, he was posthumously honored as Prince Wen, with temple name Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin received the throne, he was posthumously honored as Prince Wen, with temple name Taizu.

sentences.zh: 武成元年，追尊為文皇帝。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wucheng he was posthumously honored as Emperor Wen.
translations.idiomatic: In Wucheng year one he was posthumously honored as Emperor Wen.

sentences.zh: 帝知人善任使，從諫如順流。

translations.literal: The Emperor knew men and employed them well; he accepted remonstrance as readily as water flows downstream.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor knew men and employed them well; he accepted remonstrance as readily as water flows downstream.

sentences.zh: 崇尚儒術，明達政事，恩信被物。

translations.literal: He honored Confucian learning, was clear in government affairs, and his kindness and trust extended to all.
translations.idiomatic: He honored Confucian learning, was clear in government, and his kindness and trust reached all men.

sentences.zh: 能駕馭英豪，一見之者，咸思用命。

translations.literal: He could command heroes; all who met him wished to serve him with their lives.
translations.idiomatic: He could command heroes; all who met him wished to serve him with their lives.

sentences.zh: 沙苑所獲囚俘，釋而用之；

translations.literal: Prisoners captured at Shawei were released and employed;
translations.idiomatic: Prisoners captured at Shawei were released and employed;

sentences.zh: 及河橋之役，以充戰士，皆得其死力。

translations.literal: at the battle of Heqiao they served as fighting men and all fought to the death.
translations.idiomatic: at Heqiao they served as fighting men and all fought to the death.

sentences.zh: 諸將出征，授以方略，無不制勝。

translations.literal: When the generals went on campaign, he gave them strategy, and none failed to win.
translations.idiomatic: When generals went on campaign, he gave them strategy, and none failed to win.

sentences.zh: 性好樸素，不尚虛飾，恒以反風俗復古始為心云。

translations.literal: By nature he loved simplicity and did not value empty display; he always took it to heart to reverse custom and restore antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he loved simplicity and scorned empty display; he always sought to reverse custom and restore antiquity.

sentences.zh: 孝閔皇帝諱覺，字陀羅尼，文帝第三子也。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaomin, taboo name Jue, style name Tuoluoni, was the third son of Emperor Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaomin, taboo name Jue, style name Tuoluoni, was the third son of Emperor Wen.

sentences.zh: 母曰元皇后。

translations.literal: His mother was Empress Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was Empress Yuan.

sentences.zh: 大統八年，生於同州。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Datong he was born at Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Datong year eight he was born at Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 七歲封略陽郡公。

translations.literal: At seven he was enfeoffed as Duke of Lueyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: At seven he was enfeoffed as Duke of Lueyang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 時善相者史元華見帝，退謂所親曰：「此公子有至貴相，但恨不壽耳。」

translations.literal: At that time the physiognomist Shi Yuanhua saw the Emperor and, withdrawing, said to those close to him: "This young lord has the countenance of supreme nobility, but I regret he will not live long."
translations.idiomatic: The physiognomist Shi Yuanhua saw the Emperor and, withdrawing, told those close to him, "This young lord has the countenance of supreme nobility, but I regret he will not live long."

sentences.zh: 魏恭帝三年三月，命為安定公世子。

translations.literal: In the third month of the third year of Emperor Gong of Wei he was appointed heir of the Duke of Anding.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Wei Emperor Gong year three he was appointed heir of the Duke of Anding.

sentences.zh: 四月，拜大將軍。

translations.literal: In the fourth month he was appointed Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month he was appointed Grand General.

sentences.zh: 十月乙亥，文帝崩。

translations.literal: On the day yihai of the tenth month Emperor Wen died.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai of the tenth month Emperor Wen died.

sentences.zh: 丙子，世子嗣位為太師、大冢宰。

translations.literal: On the day bingzi the heir succeeded as Grand Preceptor and Grand Minister.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi the heir succeeded as Grand Preceptor and Grand Minister.

sentences.zh: 十二月丁亥，魏帝詔以岐陽地封帝為周公。

translations.literal: On the day dinghai of the twelfth month the Wei Emperor issued an edict enfeoffing the Emperor as Duke of Zhou with the territory of Qiyang.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai of the twelfth month the Wei Emperor enfeoffed the Emperor as Duke of Zhou with the territory of Qiyang.

sentences.zh: 庚子，詔禪位於帝曰：「予聞皇天之命不於常，惟歸於德。

translations.literal: On the day gengzi an edict abdicated the throne to the Emperor, saying: "I have heard that the mandate of Heaven is not fixed, but returns to the virtuous.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi an edict abdicated the throne to the Emperor, saying, "I have heard that Heaven's mandate is not fixed, but returns to the virtuous.

sentences.zh: 故堯授舜，舜授禹，時宜也。

translations.literal: Therefore Yao gave the throne to Shun, and Shun to Yu; that was the proper time.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore Yao gave the throne to Shun, and Shun to Yu; that was the proper time.

sentences.zh: 天厭我魏邦，垂變以告，惟爾罔弗知。

translations.literal: Heaven has grown weary of our state of Wei and sent down change to announce it; you alone did not know.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven has grown weary of Wei and sent down change to announce it; you alone did not know.

sentences.zh: 予雖不明，敢弗龔天命，格有德哉。

translations.literal: Though I am not bright, how dare I not respect Heaven's mandate and turn to the virtuous?
translations.idiomatic: Though I am not bright, how dare I not respect Heaven's mandate and turn to the virtuous?

sentences.zh: 今踵唐、虞舊典，禪位於周，庸布告爾焉。

translations.literal: Now, following the old precedent of Tang and Yu, I abdicate the throne to Zhou; let this be proclaimed to you all.
translations.idiomatic: Now, following the old precedent of Tang and Yu, I abdicate the throne to Zhou; let this be proclaimed to you all.

sentences.zh: 」使大宗伯趙貴持節奉冊書曰：「咨爾周公，帝王之位弗常，有德者受命，時乃天道。

translations.literal: " He sent Grand Master of Ceremonies Zhao Gui, Bearer of the Staff, with the book of investiture, saying: "I address you, Duke of Zhou: the throne of emperor and king is not fixed; the virtuous receive the mandate; such is Heaven's way.
translations.idiomatic: " He sent Grand Master of Ceremonies Zhao Gui, Bearer of the Staff, with the book of investiture, saying, "I address you, Duke of Zhou: the throne is not fixed; the virtuous receive the mandate; such is Heaven's way.

sentences.zh: 予式時庸，荒求於唐、虞之彜踵，曰我魏德之終舊矣。

translations.literal: I follow the time and the task, seeking far and wide the pattern of Tang and Yu, and say: the virtue of our Wei has reached its end.
translations.idiomatic: I follow the time and the task, seeking the pattern of Tang and Yu, and say: the virtue of Wei has reached its end.

sentences.zh: 我邦小大罔弗知，今其可亢怫於天道而不歸有德歟。

translations.literal: Great and small in our state all know it; how can we now resist Heaven's way and not turn to the virtuous?
translations.idiomatic: Great and small in our state all know it; how can we resist Heaven's way and not turn to the virtuous?

sentences.zh: 時用詢謀，僉曰：公昭考文公，格勛德於天地，丕濟黔黎。

translations.literal: When I consulted the times, all said: your late father Duke Wen established merit and virtue between Heaven and Earth and greatly succored the black-haired people.
translations.idiomatic: When I consulted the times, all said: your late father Duke Wen established merit and virtue between Heaven and Earth and greatly succored the people.

sentences.zh: 洎公，又躬宣重光。

translations.literal: Down to you, you again personally spread this renewed glory.
translations.idiomatic: Down to you, you again personally spread this renewed glory.

sentences.zh: 故玄象征見於上，謳訟奔走於下，天之歷數，用實在焉，予安敢弗若。

translations.literal: Therefore the dark symbols appeared above and songs of praise ran below; Heaven's count truly rests with you; how dare I not yield?
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the dark symbols appeared above and songs of praise ran below; Heaven's count truly rests with you; how dare I not yield?

sentences.zh: 是以欽祗聖典，遜位於公。

translations.literal: Therefore with reverence I respect the sacred canon and yield the throne to you.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore with reverence I respect the sacred canon and yield the throne to you.

sentences.zh: 公其享茲天命，保有萬國，可不慎歟。

translations.literal: Receive this mandate of Heaven, preserve the myriad states, and be careful.
translations.idiomatic: Receive this mandate of Heaven, preserve the myriad states, and be careful.

sentences.zh: 」魏帝臨朝，遣戶部中大夫、濟北公元迪致皇帝璽綬。

translations.literal: The Wei Emperor attended court and sent Director of the Household Bureau, Duke of Jibei Yuan Di, to present the imperial seal and cord.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei Emperor attended court and sent Director of the Household Bureau, Duke of Jibei Yuan Di, to present the imperial seal and cord.

sentences.zh: 帝固辭，公卿百辟勸進，太史陳祥瑞，乃從之。

translations.literal: The Emperor firmly declined; the dukes, ministers, and hundred officials urged him to ascend; the Grand Astrologer reported auspicious signs; he then accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor firmly declined; the dukes, ministers, and hundred officials urged him to ascend; the Grand Astrologer reported auspicious signs; he then accepted.

sentences.zh: 是日，魏帝遜位於大司馬府。

translations.literal: That day the Wei Emperor abdicated at the Grand Marshal's residence.
translations.idiomatic: That day the Wei Emperor abdicated at the Grand Marshal's residence.

sentences.zh: 元年春正月，天王即位，柴燎告天，朝百官於路門。

translations.literal: In the first month of the first year, on the day of the Heavenly King's accession, he burned firewood and reported to Heaven, and attended upon the hundred officials at Lum Gate.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of year one, on the day of the Heavenly King's accession, he burned firewood and reported to Heaven, and attended upon the hundred officials at Lum Gate.

sentences.zh: 追尊皇考文公為文王，皇妣為文後，大赦。

translations.literal: He posthumously honored his late father Duke Wen as Prince Wen and his late mother as Empress Wen, and proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: He posthumously honored his late father Duke Wen as Prince Wen and his late mother as Empress Wen, and proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 封魏帝為宋公。

translations.literal: The Wei Emperor was enfeoffed as Duke of Song.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei Emperor was enfeoffed as Duke of Song.

sentences.zh: 是日，槐里獻赤雀。

translations.literal: That day Huaili presented a red sparrow.
translations.idiomatic: That day Huaili presented a red sparrow.

sentences.zh: 百官奏議曰：「帝王之興，罔弗更正朔，明受之於天，革人視聽也。

translations.literal: The hundred officials memorialized, saying: "Whenever emperors and kings rise, none fail to correct the calendar; it makes clear that they receive it from Heaven and change what the people see and hear.
translations.idiomatic: The hundred officials memorialized, saying, "Whenever emperors and kings rise, none fail to correct the calendar; it makes clear that they receive it from Heaven and change what the people see and hear.

sentences.zh: 逮於尼甫，稽諸陰陽，雲行夏之時，後王所不易。

translations.literal: Down to Confucius, when he examined yin and yang, he said to follow the seasons of Xia; later kings did not change this.
translations.idiomatic: Down to Confucius, when he examined yin and yang, he said to follow the seasons of Xia; later kings did not change this.

sentences.zh: 今魏歷告終，周室受命；

translations.literal: Now the calendar of Wei has reached its end, and the house of Zhou receives the mandate;
translations.idiomatic: Now the calendar of Wei has reached its end, and the house of Zhou receives the mandate;

sentences.zh: 以木承水，實當行錄；

translations.literal: using wood to succeed water, green is truly the color to be employed;
translations.idiomatic: using wood to succeed water, green is truly the color to be employed;

sentences.zh: 正用夏時，式遵聖道。

translations.literal: correctly using the Xia calendar, we follow the sage way.
translations.idiomatic: correctly using the Xia calendar, we follow the sage way.

sentences.zh: 惟文王誕玄氣之祥，有黑水之讖，服色宜尚烏。

translations.literal: Prince Wen bore the auspice of dark vapor and the prophecy of black water; ceremonial colors should honor black.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Wen bore the auspice of dark vapor and the prophecy of black water; ceremonial colors should honor black.

sentences.zh: 制曰：「可。

translations.literal: The decree said: "Approved.
translations.idiomatic: The decree said, "Approved.

sentences.zh: 」以大司徒、趙郡王李弼為太師；

translations.literal: " Grand Minister of Education, Prince of Zhao Commandery Li Bi, was made Grand Preceptor;
translations.idiomatic: " Grand Minister of Education, Prince of Zhao Commandery Li Bi, was made Grand Preceptor;

sentences.zh: 以大宗伯、南陽公趙貴為太傅、大冢宰；

translations.literal: Grand Master of Ceremonies, Duke of Nanyang Zhao Gui, was made Grand Tutor and Grand Minister;
translations.idiomatic: Grand Master of Ceremonies, Duke of Nanyang Zhao Gui, was made Grand Tutor and Grand Minister;

sentences.zh: 以大司馬、河內公獨孤信為太保；

translations.literal: Grand Marshal, Duke of Henei Dugu Xin, was made Grand Guardian;
translations.idiomatic: Grand Marshal, Duke of Henei Dugu Xin, was made Grand Guardian;

sentences.zh: 以大宗伯、中山公護為大司馬；

translations.literal: Grand Master of Ceremonies, Duke of Zhongshan Hu, was made Grand Marshal;
translations.idiomatic: Grand Master of Ceremonies, Duke of Zhongshan Hu, was made Grand Marshal;

sentences.zh: 以大將軍寧都公毓、高陽公達奚武、武陽公豆盧寧、小司冠陽平公李遠、小司馬博陵公賀蘭禪、小宗伯魏安公尉迥等並為柱國。

translations.literal: Grand General Duke of Ningdu Yu, Duke of Gaoyang Daxi Wu, Duke of Wuyang Dou Lu'ning, Lesser Director of the Court Duke of Yangping Li Yuan, Lesser Grand Marshal Duke of Boling Helan Chan, Lesser Master of Ceremonies Duke of Wei'an Wei Chiji, and others were all made Pillars of State.
